evidence.text: IFC's fund ALAC filed a fresh Form 144 on 2026-09-01 to sell a further 857,362 LSAK shares (exactly the Rule 144 1%-of-outstanding cap, ~10.3x the baseline 20-day ADV of 83,297) starting 2026-09-02 through J.P. Morgan, after selling 857,362 shares between 2026-06-08 and 2026-08-07 and 808,737 shares between 2026-03-05 and 2026-04-17 — i.e. the seller was capped out and absent from the tape from 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-01 and returns to it in the same week as the print.
evidence.why_not_priced: International Finance Corp stopped filing Form 4s on 2026-04-16 because the IFC group fell to 9.84% of the class (Schedule 13D/A, 2026-06-17: 3,271,862 + 1,856,263 + 3,302,551 = 8,430,676 shares), so every insider-transaction screen that feeds Benzinga/MarketBeat/Fintel now shows LSAK with no insider selling for five months while 771k+ shares were in fact distributed after 22 June. The last 20 sessions of tape carry no information about this supply at all, because ALAC's own filing shows it made zero sales between 08/07 and the 09/01 refiling. If the market had it, you would see it in the positioning: short interest is 0.28% of shares out and total option open interest in the baseline is 115 contracts with a put/call OI ratio of 0.01 — there is literally no expression of a supply overhang in the price. Mechanism into the measurement window: a 144 programme worked as a percentage of volume puts its largest absolute supply on the highest-volume session of the quarter, which is the reaction session.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by a different filing type from the same filer family — Schedule 13D/A Amendment No. 5 discloses 671,112 shares sold by ALAC between 2026-03-18 and 2026-06-17 at $4.65-$5.44 across 24 dates (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041514/000119312526274718/0001193125-26-274718.txt, 2026-06-17), and the Form 4 by International Finance Corp dated 2026-04-13 confirms the same entity was a Section 16 insider until April (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041514/000119312526153395/0001193125-26-153395-index.htm). These are one source cluster — same seller, three filing types — and should be collapsed as such; nothing from an unrelated party points the same way.

evidence.text: Nine-month FY2026 GAAP net loss attributable to Lesaka is -$461 thousand (nine months to 2026-03-31, per the company's own Q3 statement of operations), so management's repeated promise of 'the first year we will be profitable since the creation of Lesaka four years ago' rests entirely on Q4 FY26 clearing +$0.46m — in the quarter that carries the 30 June annual goodwill impairment test on R3,532,856 thousand (~$207m) of goodwill against $186.6m of total equity.
evidence.why_not_priced: Exactly one Wall Street analyst publishes a target on LSAK ($8 against a $4.57 spot), so there is no published GAAP net-income consensus for the wire to compare the print against and no model that has done this addition in public. The 'delivers on guidance' framing has been repeated all year and is what the coverage reflects; if the market had focused on the arithmetic it would treat 'net income: positive' as a Q4-dependent binary rather than as banked, and you would see some downside hedging — instead put open interest is effectively nil. Lesaka has produced a negative year-end accounting surprise in each of the last two cycles (FY2025: $49.3m MobiKwik loss plus $18.4m impairments and an agent-to-principal revenue restatement disclosed with the FY25 preliminary; and a headline-earnings restatement filed 2026-05-18), and Q3 FY26 alone already absorbed ~ZAR 104m of impairments and one-offs.
evidence.independence: Separate document, separate filer: the 2026-05-18 8-K/SENS correcting previously published Q3 FY2026 headline earnings (Q3 FY2025 restated from a $(5,391)k to a $(22,362)k headline loss) evidences the recurring year-end accounting-quality issue independently of the Q3 income statement — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041514/000106299326002769/exhibit99-1.htm, 2026-05-18.

evidence.text: Management pre-committed on the 2026-05-07 Q3 call that tonight's release carries FY2027 guidance plus a first-ever three-year medium-term outlook 'inclusive of Bank Zero' — but Bank Zero is still unclosed (long-stop extended 2026-06-11 from 2026-08-06 to 2027-01-31 with Prudential Authority and exchange-control consents outstanding, and no completion 8-K on EDGAR as of 2026-09-09), it issues ~12% of Lesaka's fully diluted shares plus up to R91m cash, and Lesaka's own framing is that Bank Zero only becomes profitable in the fiscal year AFTER completion.
evidence.why_not_priced: Genuinely two-sided and I am sizing it small for that reason. Downside: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance is ZAR 5.50-6.00 after two years of >100% and ~150% growth; 12% more shares alone takes a 30%-growth FY2027 from ~ZAR 7.4 to ~ZAR 6.6 before a loss-making bank is consolidated, so the FY27 guide can print near-flat on a stock that has been marked on a doubling cadence. Upside: a first-ever three-year outlook is a confidence-signalling device management would not volunteer into a weak plan. With one covering analyst and no published ZAR FY2027 consensus, there is no anchor either way — which is exactly why the price cannot already contain it; a market that had priced this would show a dispersion trade or at least a two-sided option chain, and the chain has 115 contracts of total open interest.
evidence.independence: The unclosed status and outstanding Prudential Authority / exchange-control consents are corroborated from a different source and document — https://www.citizen.co.za/business/lesaka-pushes-bank-zero-acquisition-deadline-to-2027-as-regulatory-approvals-lag/ (2026-06-18) and the 8-K disclosing the long-stop extension (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/LSAK/8-k-lesaka-technologies-inc-reports-material-event-8d4a61395f12.html, 8-K dated 2026-06-11, accepted 2026-06-17). The FY27/medium-term-outlook commitment and the 12% dilution reading both come from the same Q3 call transcript, so treat that half as one source.

evidence.text: JSE SENS trading statement: no 2026 trading statement for LSK found. SENS archives were unreadable or empty (sharedata.co.za News.aspx returned only chrome, sharenet sens_bycompany 404, moneyweb click-a-company 403, ir.lesakatech.com/sec-sens.php renders no list). The only 2026 SENS items surfaced by search are the Q1/Q2/Q3 results, the directors'-dealings notices, the executive-chairman compensation amendment, the 2026-05-18 headline-earnings correction and the 2026-08-26 results-date notice — no trading statement and no cautionary.
No preliminary pre-release: EDGAR submissions show no 8-K after 2026-08-03 (option-award shareholder vote) and none since, so unlike FY2025 there has been no early leak of FY2026 numbers.
No Bank Zero completion announcement as of 2026-09-09.
No officer/director Form 4 activity since 2026-04-16 — no insider buying or selling signal from management itself.
Short interest 0.28% of shares outstanding (2026-08-28) — no crowded position, no squeeze fuel, no information.

Bank Zero standalone financials: no published loss figure for a South African mutual bank of this size could be sourced, so the FY27 earnings drag could not be quantified beyond the ~12% share dilution.

No supplier, customer, franchisee, landlord or competitor gave guidance after Lesaka last spoke (2026-05-07) that bears specifically on Lesaka's April-June quarter; SA consumer-credit and fuel-shock data (inflation to 5.0% in June 2026 on the Hormuz oil shock) is macro and visible to everyone.

The company discloses both currencies prominently and quoted Q3 ZAR revenue as +0.2% YoY, so this is disclosed rather than hidden and I did not file it as a finding.
App-store review volume, hiring pages, status pages and customer forums: pursued but produced no datum specific and dated enough to carry a URL.

evidence.text: FY27 guidance requires a four-point inflection in the revenue trend starting in the quarter being reported: FY26 total revenue was $512.7m less $108.9m of Global Knowledge equals ~$403.8m of continuing (TDS) revenue, so the $388-406m FY27 guide brackets flat; Q1 FY27 was $94.5m, -4.7% YoY, which leaves the guide midpoint needing Q2-Q4 at about -0.7% versus a Q1 running at -4.7% and a company that itself flagged 'softness in government bookings' and consumer down 21%.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is effectively no sell-side model on this name to embed the bridge. Market cap is ~$60m (8.97m shares at $6.66), 20-day average volume is 44,231 shares (~$295k/day), there is no listed option chain at all, and the only rating action reported in August was Weiss Ratings — an algorithmic service — moving from 'sell (e+)' to 'sell (d-)'. If the market had done this arithmetic there would be a published Q2-Q4 revenue bridge and a visible estimate cut after the June 9 reaffirmation; instead the calendar carries a single estimate. The GK divestiture leg of the arithmetic is priced (the guide already excludes GK); the required inflection is not.
evidence.independence: Company's own Q1 FY27 release and call give the -4.7%/-21% consumer/government-softness inputs (https://investor.skillsoft.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/453/skillsoft-reports-financial-results-for-the-first-quarter-of-fiscal-2027, 2026-06-09), and the FY26 base is from the Q4 FY26 release (https://investor.skillsoft.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/447/skillsoft-reports-financial-results-for-the-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-of-fiscal-2026, 2026-04-07). S&P independently models 'fiscal 2027 revenues near $400 million', i.e. the bottom half of the guide.

evidence.text: Q2 FY27 (May 1 - Jul 31, 2026) is new CFO Ron Kisling's first full quarter — he started 2026-05-20, twenty days before the June 9 reaffirmation — and his predecessor John Frederick's transition-advisory contract expired 2026-09-04, five days before this print, so the first quarter he can fully own is the first one reported without the author of the inherited guidance still under contract.
evidence.why_not_priced: The wire reported 'Skillsoft appoints new CFO' in May and moved on; what it did not report is the calendar arithmetic — that the outgoing CFO's advisory engagement was written to end September 4 and this print is September 9. Nobody has published the Kisling-inherits-Frederick's-guide framing. If it were priced you would see it in a preview note; there are no covering previews on a $60m nano-cap with no options.
evidence.independence: Partly overlapping with finding 1 — this is the same outcome (a guidance reset) via different evidence, so I have sized it only as the incremental probability shift, not as a standalone -6%. Scorer should treat findings 1 and 2 as one bet with two sources. Confirming detail on Frederick's September 4 end date: https://investor.skillsoft.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/451/skillsoft-appoints-ron-kisling-as-chief-financial-officer (2026-05-20).

evidence.text: The two enterprise-learning comps that reported after Skillsoft last spoke on June 9 disagree with each other, and the closer pure-play comp is the positive one: Docebo (2026-08-07) reported ARR +9.5% YoY, a second consecutive quarter of re-acceleration, and RAISED full-year revenue guidance by $3.5m citing enterprise strength, while Coursera (2026-07-29) reported enterprise NRR down to 91% on L&D budget pressure.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sweep row correctly notes the 'corporate-learning-disrupted-by-AI' bear case is fully written up and standing. What is written up is the thesis, not a test of it — and the post-June-9 evidence fails to confirm it. If the market had processed Docebo's raise as a read-across, SKIL would not have fallen 29% over the same 20 days into a print with no offsetting company-specific news. I file this as a small positive precisely because the negative leg (Coursera) exists and I am netting them rather than filing only the leg that suits me.
evidence.independence: The offsetting negative leg is Coursera's Q2, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729966984/en/Coursera-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results (2026-07-29, date verified from the URL path 20260729). Both dates verified from URL paths, not snippets.

evidence.text: Tonight is the first call at which a refinancing update is contractually due: on 2026-06-09 Hovsepian said addressing the debt maturities becomes 'management's top financial priority' once the Global Knowledge sale closes, and it closed 2026-07-06 — a $574.6m term loan due 2028-07-16 against $115.6m cash and a ~$60m equity, so any constructive statement is worth far more in percentage terms than silence costs.
evidence.why_not_priced: The asymmetry, not the fact, is the finding. The bad branch is already in the tape: the -29.22% 20-day run-up starts within a day of the S&P downgrade to CCC+/negative, which was explicitly about refinancing risk into the 2028 maturity. A market that had also priced a constructive branch would not have this equity at 4.5x EV/EBITDA on the company's own $108-116m guide. With no option chain there is no skew to fade and no volatility premium being paid for the branch, so I score it as a positive-mean, very-wide-band event rather than a direction.

evidence.text: Caleres reported 2026-09-09 that Famous Footwear comparable sales fell 5.9% in the quarter ended 2026-08-01 — the identical fiscal window to SHOE's Q2 — blaming 'a later Back-to-School season and softness in lifestyle athletic'; Famous Footwear comped -2.3% in Q1 against Shoe Carnival's -2.1%, so the two banners were running in lockstep before this 360bp step-down, while SHOE's Q2 revenue consensus of $299.19m implies only about -2.4% YoY.
evidence.why_not_priced: Caleres' headline was an EPS beat and a raised floor, and CAL traded up on it; SHOE closed -0.67% on the day the datapoint landed and is still up 4.1% over five sessions. If the market had read the Famous Footwear line as a comp read-through, SHOE would have broken its 52-week low of $12.78 on 09-09 rather than sitting a fraction above it, and the sell-side note flow would show Q2 revenue cuts after 09-09 rather than the last visible action being a Williams Trading target cut dated ~09-02 that still carries a Buy. Both causes Caleres named are channel-wide, not company-specific, and SHOE is more exposed to them than Famous Footwear: management said on the Q1 call that back-to-school 'begins the third week of July, and it really is an August play' and that '70% of our business is still athletic during that time period' — a later back-to-school and soft lifestyle athletic hit precisely SHOE's Q2 mix.
evidence.independence: Genesco, quarter also ended 2026-08-01, reported 2026-09-03 that consolidated comps fell 1% and that it CUT its full-year comp guidance to flat from +1-2%, corroborating that the May-July window itself was weak in footwear retail: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018498/000119312526381023/gco-ex99_1.htm . Management's own 70%-athletic and August-play quotes are from a third document, the 2026-05-21 Q1 call transcript: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/21/shoe-carnival-scvl-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/

evidence.text: SHOE has no IEEPA tariff-refund windfall available to cushion the quarter — its 10-K states 'Substantially all of our footwear product is manufactured overseas, including the merchandise we purchase from domestic vendors and the smaller portion we import directly from overseas manufacturers', so it is importer of record on only a small slice, whereas Caleres booked $55.6m of IEEPA recoveries plus $1.8m interest in the very quarter whose beat is being read across to SHOE.
evidence.why_not_priced: SHOE's Q1 10-Q filed 2026-06-05 carries no tariff receivable and the 2026-05-21 call spoke of tariffs only as ongoing 'average unit cost pressures' — three months after the Supreme Court struck IEEPA on 2026-02-20 and a month after CBP opened the CAPE refund process. If the market expected a refund, the stock would not be making 52-week lows into a print with $116m of cash and a debt-free balance sheet, and the FY gross margin guide of ~34% (-260bp) would have been challenged as stale rather than reaffirmed unremarked. The asymmetry is the point: the part of Caleres' print SHOE shares is the retail banner that comped -5.9%, and the parts that produced the beat — the refund and a +23.6% brand portfolio — SHOE does not have, which also removes the mechanism Caleres used to lift its full-year floor.
evidence.independence: SOURCE CLUSTER NOTE: the $55.6m refund figure comes from the same Caleres 8-K as finding 1 and should be collapsed with it; the load-bearing, independent element here is the 10-K sourcing language and the absence of any tariff receivable in the Q1 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000895447/000119312526258362/scvl-20260502.htm (filed 2026-06-05).

evidence.text: The same later-back-to-school shift that damages SHOE's Q2 lands squarely in its Q3: Genesco said on 2026-09-03 that Journeys accelerated to a mid-single-digit comp in August and raised its FY EPS outlook to the high end, and Caleres said Famous Footwear comps are flat quarter-to-date through Labor Day — a 590bp sequential improvement — so SHOE, whose FY2026 guide of $1.40-$1.60 was explicitly framed as 'down first half and then up second half', has a credible constructive August update to give from a 52-week low.
evidence.why_not_priced: SHOE fell from $16.11 on 08-10 to $12.84 on 09-01, -20% on no company news at all — no 8-K since 06-11 and no Form 4 since 06-22 — which is the market pricing a bad quarter without pricing the offsetting Q3 handoff. If the August handoff were priced, SHOE would not be trading within 4% of its 52-week low three sessions after the two most comparable retailers both described August as materially better than May-July. This is the mechanism by which a revenue miss can still produce an up day, exactly as it did for CAL on 09-09.
evidence.independence: Caleres' 'quarter to date through Labor Day, Famous Footwear comparable store sales are flat' is in a different filing, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000014707/000001470726000138/cal-20260909xex99d1.htm (2026-09-09) — note this is the same document as finding 1 and points the opposite way, which is why finding 1 is sized below the raw comp read-through.

evidence.text: The baseline's put/call open-interest ratio of 26.6 on 28,591 contracts is a data artifact, not a positioning signal: the actual 2026-09-18 chain carries open interest in the hundreds, roughly 488 puts against 309 calls across the strikes shown, a ratio near 1.6.

evidence.text: MasterCraft's board changed the fiscal year end from June 30 to December 31 effective 1 July 2026, so there is no fiscal 2027 - the next reporting period is a six-month transition period (1 Jul to 31 Dec 2026) filed on Form 10-KT, meaning any forward guidance given on 10 September is a stub covering only MasterCraft's seasonally weakest half, not the annual range the market is set up to trade.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was an Item 5.03 8-K with no press release and no wire pickup beyond one automated Globe and Mail stub; if the market had absorbed it, aggregators would carry transition-period estimates instead of showing FY2027 (Jun-2027) as 'Data unavailable' on stockanalysis.com, and the day's own sweep brief would not have written 'this is a Q4 print, so initial FY2027 guidance is the event.' The optical hazard is concrete: MCFT's Jul-Dec half ran $69.0m + ~$69m of net sales in FY26 against $78.2m and ~$93m in the Jan-Jun half, so a six-month guide will print an EPS and EBITDA headline roughly a third of an annual number against an FY26 adjusted EPS anchor of $1.65.
evidence.independence: The pro-forma 8-K/A confirms the acquired company (Marine Products) was a 31-December filer, which is the benign reason for the change and independently corroborates the calendar realignment: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1129155/000110465926056635/mpx-20260507xex99d1.htm

evidence.text: The published quarterly consensus is not a forecast of the company that will report - $93.05m revenue is exactly MasterCraft's own standalone FY26 guide of $312m less the $218.967m it had already booked in nine months, and $0.622 EPS is exactly $1.65 less $1.03, while the company explicitly said that outlook 'does not include the pending combination with Marine Products' and then consolidated Chaparral and Robalo from 15 May, roughly 6.5 weeks of the quarter, at an MPX run-rate of $66.5m per quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the quarterly consensus were merger-adjusted it would not sit within $0.02m of a subtraction the company itself published four months ago; and the same vendors' annual line is internally inconsistent with it (stockanalysis FY26 revenue of $338.25m implies a $119.3m Q4, versus the $93.05m quarterly figure), which is the signature of a stale quarterly row nobody rebuilt. Consequence is a split wire headline on a name that trades 161k shares a day: revenue roughly $120-126m against $93m est (+30%), while weighted diluted shares go from 16.28m to about 20.2m for the quarter, so adjusted EPS lands near $0.55 and reads as an EPS miss. I size it small and two-sided because the direction of the net headline is genuinely ambiguous.
evidence.independence: MPX's own last standalone quarter, $66.5m of net sales for Jan-Mar 2026 at 16.6% gross margin and a GAAP net loss, sizes the stub and shows why it adds revenue but almost no EPS: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1129155/000110465926056635/mpx-20260507xex99d1.htm

evidence.text: US retail registrations on a 12-month rolling basis through June 2026, published 2 September, show the four categories the merged MasterCraft actually competes in are the four weakest in the market - towboats 7,529 units down 9.9%, runabouts 13,261 down 11.4%, pontoons 47,119 down 6.6%, saltwater fishboats 21,523 down 2.8% - against a total market down 3.5% carried by freshwater fishing (+0.4%), while MasterCraft's own nine-month FY26 net sales rose 7.0% to $218.967m on 'higher unit volumes', i.e. it shipped into a channel that was contracting at roughly triple its stated wholesale growth.
evidence.why_not_priced: The read-across everyone did was the wrong one: Brunswick raised FY guidance on a US pipeline down ~1,300 units and Malibu's Q4 net sales rose 42.7% with the stock up 12%, but Malibu's growth is Saxdor (European outboard) and its legacy FY27 guide is only low-to-mid single digit - neither peer's tailwind maps onto towboats, runabouts and pontoons. If the market had priced MCFT's specific mix it would not be sitting on a -6.2% twenty-day run-up with sell-side targets of $25-$30 raised into a sector rally, and there would be a note reconciling a +7% wholesale build against a -9.9% towboat retail number. The transition-period guide is the first moment the company has to reconcile the two.
evidence.independence: Different document, different company: Marine Products - now roughly a third of the combined entity - disclosed field unit inventory only 2% below the prior year at the end of Q1 2026, i.e. it had not destocked at all, in direct contrast to Brunswick's lean pipeline commentary. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1129155/000110465926056635/mpx-20260507xex99d1.htm  (Note: this same MPX release is also cited in finding 2, for the unrelated fact of its revenue run-rate; the two readings share one document and should be collapsed to one source.)

evidence.text: Kewaunee ran a book-to-bill of roughly 0.83 for all of FY26 -- consolidated backlog fell $214.6m -> $205.0m -> $192.9m -> $183.2m -> $165.9m across five straight quarters (an accelerating burn, -$17.3m in Q4 alone) while quarterly revenue was held flat at $71.1m / $70.1m / $69.4m / $71.4m -- and the FY26 10-K states 'not less than 90% of our order backlog at April 30, 2026 will be shipped during fiscal year 2027', i.e. >=$149m of shipments from backlog against $282m of FY26 revenue; with FY26 opex of $63.7m (~$15.9m/quarter, largely fixed) and a 28.5% gross margin, breakeven revenue is ~$56m per quarter, so Q1 FY27 revenue anywhere in the $55-63m range against the $71.1m year-ago comp puts EPS near zero versus $1.04.
evidence.why_not_priced: If this arithmetic were priced there would be a published FY27 revenue estimate below $240m and a sell-side note on the operating-leverage cliff; instead stockanalysis.com shows 'Analyst Forecast: Not available', the sweep found a single estimate, there is no conference call and no option chain, and the stock trades ~2,000 shares a day (368 shares today). Most tellingly, the 2026-06-23 release that disclosed the single largest backlog drop of the cycle produced only a -3.63% reaction, versus -21.23% and -13.08% on prior, smaller backlog disappointments -- that is not a market that has run the conversion math. And the stock at $36.01 is 11.2x trailing $3.22, which is not a multiple that embeds an EPS collapse.
evidence.independence: The backlog chain comes from four separate 8-K exhibits rather than one document: Q1 FY26 ($205.0m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552925000033/prfy26q1earningsrelease.htm , Q2 FY26 ($192.9m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552925000051/prfy26q2earningsrelease.htm , Q3 FY26 ($183.2m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552926000006/prfy26q3earningsrelease.htm , Q4 FY26 ($165.9m, LPG $118.8m / International $47.1m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552926000017/prfy26q4earningsrelease.htm . Note that the >=90% shipment statement and the $165.9m level are the same underlying fact as the Q4 release, so the 10-K and the Q4 8-K should be collapsed to one source; the four-quarter revenue-flat-while-backlog-falls series is the genuinely additive part.

evidence.text: US hot-rolled coil, the primary input to Kewaunee's steel laboratory casework and fume hoods, rose from ~$1,070/short ton at the start of Kewaunee's fiscal Q1 FY27 (SMU average, week of 2026-05-01) to $1,180/st by 2026-08-12, a four-year high with Section 232 at 50% -- a ~10% sequential input-cost step inside a quarter whose revenue is delivered against fixed-price project backlog booked 6-18 months earlier.
evidence.why_not_priced: Steel prices are public but nobody maps them onto a $103m lab-furniture microcap with no analyst model; if this link were being made there would be a gross-margin-driven estimate cut, and there is no estimate to cut. evidence.text: The entire CBP IEEPA-refund filing wave landed inside Descartes' May-July quarter -- CAPE Phase 1 deployed 2026-04-20, Phase 2 on 2026-06-29, Phase 3 late July -- against ~53 million entries and ~330,000 importers, and Descartes sells the batch Post-Summary-Correction automation and duty-recovery service that brokers need to work those entries at scale, so the customs-transaction line likely beat the $169.0m Q2 baseline by more than its usual margin.
evidence.why_not_priced: The wire frame on DSGX is that the February 2026 Supreme Court strike-down of IEEPA tariffs removes trade complexity and therefore demand -- that is the frame that took the stock 30% off its high and left puts bid. If the market had worked through the mechanics it would see the opposite for this one quarter: unwinding $166bn of duties across 53m entries is itself a one-time filing surge, and it fell precisely in the May-July window. With only two published estimates there is no model that carries a PSC-volume line, and Descartes' guidance construct (a $169.0m contracted 'baseline' plus whatever transactional volume arrives) means this shows up exactly in the beat-over-baseline, which is the number the stock trades on.
evidence.independence: Descartes' own product page for the refund wave describes automating 'every step of the PSC lifecycle' and 'batch PSC filing, allowing thousands of entries to be processed simultaneously' (https://www.descartes.com/resources/knowledge-center/tariff-refunds-ieepa-tariffs, undated page), and its 2026-04-22 news item sizes the pool at '$166 billion and more than 330,000 importers' (https://www.descartes.com/resources/news/tariff-refund-portal-launch-creates-new-cost-recovery-path-ecommerce-sellers). Caveat I will not hide: the CAPE declaration itself is a CSV upload to the ACE portal, not an ABI transaction, so Descartes' monetisation is via the PSC/duty-recovery work around it rather than the declaration -- that is why the low end of my band is below zero.

evidence.text: Descartes' own monthly container data for the quarter it is about to report: May 2026 2,428,758 TEU (+11.5% YoY), June 2,400,627 (+8.2% YoY), July 2,508,310 (-4.3% YoY) -- about +4.6% YoY for the May-July quarter -- and the report published this morning (2026-09-10) puts August at 2,603,709 TEU, +3.8% MoM, +3.3% YoY, the third-highest month on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: Genuinely two-sided and that is why I size it small: July was the first negative YoY month of 2026 and it is the last month of the reporting quarter, which argues the volume-linked line decelerated hard through the quarter; but the quarter was still +4.6% YoY and the exit rate re-accelerated to a near-record August. If the market had read Descartes' own series rather than the generic 'soft freight' headline, the stock would not be 5.25% lower over five sessions into a print whose volume backdrop is a record-adjacent August. Nobody aggregates a company's own free monthly dataset as a nowcast of its own quarter.
evidence.independence: The August figure is separately reported by IT Supply Chain, dated 2026-09-10, with the same 2,603,709 TEU and 'third-highest on record' framing (https://itsupplychain.com/august-u-s-containerized-imports-reach-third-highest-level-on-record-amid-persistent-trade-risk/). evidence.text: Descartes deployed roughly $250m of cash on four weeks of M&A around quarter-end -- Drivin $30m on 2026-07-06 (in-quarter), Tai $100m on 2026-08-24 and Extensiv $120m on 2026-09-01 (both post-quarter, eight days apart) -- and Extensiv is a distressed-timeline asset: its $80m Runway Growth senior secured term loan matured 2026-06-30, 63 days before the sale, and the price is roughly 1.2-2.4x revenue against Descartes' own 46% adjusted-EBITDA-margin base.
evidence.why_not_priced: The announcements are public and the tape sold both of them (-1.21% on 24 Aug, -2.41% on 1 Sep in the sealed baseline), so the fact of the deals is priced. What is not priced is the size: neither press release discloses revenue, EBITDA or accretion, so nothing in consensus -- two estimates -- carries a number. Descartes will for the first time calibrate a Q3 baseline that includes them on this call, and its Q2 baseline construct was $169.0m revenue / $102.5m opex / $66.5m calibration = 39%. If the incremental revenue arrives at anything like the margin implied by a 1.2-2.4x revenue price on a company whose lender's clock had run out, the headline baseline-revenue jump comes with a visible step down in that 39%. If the market had done this arithmetic the skew would be steeper than 4.63 vol points and the deals would have drawn sell-side notes quantifying the dilution; they drew none.

evidence.text: On 2026-09-02, eight days before the fiscal-year-end print and the FY2027 guidance introduction, ibex announced its first-ever entry into Egypt - a Cairo (City Stars, Nasr City) delivery centre opening in October and scaling to 1,000 employees in nine months, serving HealthTech, Technology and Retail clients - a ~3% addition to a 36,000-person workforce in a country it has never operated in.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a GlobeNewswire site-expansion release with no dollar figure attached, on a stock that trades 99k shares a day and that stockanalysis.com shows as covered by two estimating analysts whose price targets were last updated 2026-05-07 - i.e. nobody has re-cut a model since the announcement. If the market had read a brand-new offshore country plus a signed lease and live hiring as a statement about contracted FY2027 demand, the 20-day run-up would be more than +6.5%, the consensus target would not still be $37.50 against a $37.40 spot, and someone would have written it up. Companies do not commit capex and 1,000 hires into a geography with no existing client base a week before setting annual guidance unless the demand behind it is already signed.
evidence.independence: Second, separate capacity commitment three weeks earlier: on 2026-08-10 ibex said it would hire 400 more in Tegucigalpa by year-end off a ~1,200 base, with the Honduran president publicly discussing doubling or tripling the workforce - https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/10/3341871/0/en/ibex-ceo-and-honduras-president-nasry-asfura-meet-to-discuss-growth-investment-and-ongoing-partnership.html . Corroborating direction from a third source: management raised FY2026 capex guidance to $25-30M from $20-25M 'to meet increased demand in higher-margin regions' on the 2026-05-06 call.

evidence.text: USD/PHP stands at 62.63 on 2026-09-10, up 9.6% over twelve months, and averaged near 60 through IBEX's April-June quarter against roughly 57 a year earlier - a direct cost-side tailwind for a company whose offshore delivery (Philippines, Pakistan, India) produced 51.1% of nine-month FY2026 revenue and which runs eight of its ~29 delivery sites in the Philippines.
evidence.why_not_priced: The FY2027 EBITDA-margin guide is set against a hedge book that rolls onto a 62-peso rate, versus the ~56-58 embedded in FY2026. With two estimating analysts and no published revision since 2026-05-07, there is no visible model carrying a re-based FY2027 margin. If it were priced you would see an FY2027 margin whisper above the 12.8-13.1% FY2026 guided rate and a target above spot; instead the consensus target is $37.50 on a $37.40 stock. The offset - IBEX hedges forward, so the FY2026 quarter itself captures less of this than the raw rate implies - is exactly why the payload sits in the FY2027 guide rather than the printed quarter.
evidence.independence: Delivery-location revenue mix (offshore 51.1% of the nine months to 2026-03-31) comes from a different document, the Q3 FY2026 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001720420/000172042026000011/ibex-20260331.htm . evidence.text: Germanium printed 26,500 CNY/kg on 2026-09-10, up 8.16% in the past month and up 84.03% year over year, i.e. the squeeze that is the entire economic case for LightPath's germanium-free BlackDiamond glass accelerated through exactly the June quarter and through the 20 days in which LPTH fell 27.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing the germanium input, LPTH would have decoupled from the drone complex during the August unwind. It did not: on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-28 LPTH fell alongside Ondas, Unusual Machines, Red Cat and Kratos - names with zero germanium exposure and opposite YTD performance - which is the signature of positioning, not of anyone re-underwriting LightPath's input economics. A market that had priced this would show LPTH's 20-day beta to the c-UAS basket breaking down and 25-delta skew tilted to calls; instead skew is +1.21 vol points (mildly put-bid) and the stock tracked the basket point for point. evidence.text: An April 16, 2026 side letter fixed the G5 Infrared Year-2 earnout at exactly $9.0M ($6.3M cash + $2.7M stock, payable 1-15 January 2027) against a carried liability of only $6.7M at 31 March 2026 - so roughly $2.3M of additional non-cash fair-value/accretion charge is arithmetically locked into the Q4 FY26 P&L, on top of the $1.78M Amorphous Materials earnout accrual, guaranteeing a GAAP loss materially wider than the single published ($0.02) estimate and a $6.3M cash outflow four months out.
evidence.why_not_priced: With a single published EPS estimate on the name and no sell-side model visible that reconciles the side letter, the headline GAAP number that hits the wires and the algos at 16:05 ET is pre-determined to look like a large miss versus ($0.02). If this were priced there would be a visible adjusted-vs-GAAP bridge in the previews and the estimate itself would sit nearer ($0.06)-($0.09); instead the aggregators still carry ($0.02). The offset - and why I size this small rather than large - is that this base has looked through identical earnout noise before: the 11-Feb-2026 print carried a fair-value charge and the stock rose 21.5%.

evidence.text: Buried in the body of the 22 July 2026 8-K on the China divestiture - not in the press release and not in any wire story - is a five-year supply-back obligation under which the divested Zhenjiang plant sells product to LightPath at cost plus a markup that starts at 10% and steps up 5 points for every $1M of the $4.5M purchase price the buyer repays, capped at cost plus 30%, so LightPath's own input cost rises mechanically as it collects its sale proceeds.

Zhenjiang was the in-house low-cost molded-optics plant supplying the Visible Components line at internal cost; converting that to cost+10% rising to cost+30% is a structural gross-margin headwind against management's stated 40% target, which they were already guiding as slipping 'a quarter or 2'. evidence.text: Champions' FY2026 'record revenue' was entirely one customer: the same significant customer went from 13% of revenue in FY2025 to 24% in FY2026 (13% x $56.9m = $7.4m to 24% x $59.4m = $14.3m, i.e. +$6.9m) while total revenue rose only $2.5m - so every other customer combined shrank from ~$49.5m to ~$45.1m, about -8.8% - and that one customer is also 25% of the year-end receivable.
evidence.why_not_priced: The concentration disclosure exists only as a 10-K note (Significant Customers, R13); it is not in the 8-K exhibit 99.1 press release, which carries the income statement and balance sheet but no concentration table, and the word never comes up in the Q4 call, where the framing was '12% growth in TOS services ... without material additions to headcount' i.e. operating leverage. There is no published EPS consensus on this name and no sell-side model, so nobody has rebuilt the revenue bridge. If it were priced you would see the question asked in the Q4 Q&A and you would not see the stock still carrying a 'record year' narrative in every secondary write-up; you would also expect a wider discount than the -8.75% the July 27 print produced off a headline beat.
evidence.independence: Same direction from a different line of the same 10-K/press release: deferred revenue fell 43% from $15.443m to $8.828m (a multi-year low) and management attributed the FY26 operating cash drain to 'lower upfront billings' - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/771856/000162828026017345/csbr-20260131.htm (2026-03-12). NOTE: that deferred-revenue figure IS printed in the July 27 press-release balance sheet, so it is more priced than the concentration note, and I have not filed it as a separate finding precisely to avoid counting one revenue-quality story twice.

evidence.text: On June 5, 2026 - inside the quarter being reported tonight - Champions amended its Rockville, MD office/lab lease to run through March 31, 2037, adding roughly $6.3m of ROU asset and lease liability and about $16.9m of undiscounted minimum payments; the company's entire pre-existing lease book was $3.7m of ROU asset and ~$8.0m of minimum payments, against $4.87m of cash and $4.07m of total stockholders' equity.
evidence.why_not_priced: It appears in exactly one place: the 10-K subsequent-events note. It is absent from the July 27 press release (whose balance sheet is dated April 30, 2026 and therefore pre-dates it), absent from the earnings call transcript, and there is no 8-K and no press coverage of the lease at all. Tonight is the first time the numbers land on a reported balance sheet - lease liabilities roughly triple and total liabilities rise on the order of a quarter - for a company whose entire equity is $4.1m. If the market had focused on it there would be commentary tying the 11-year commitment to the radiopharmaceutical build-out, and the stock would not be flat-to-up over 20 days.
evidence.independence: Consistent with, but from a different source than, the company's continued facility/capability spend: the Aug 31, 2026 announcement of in-house SPECT/CT radiopharmaceutical imaging - https://press.championsoncology.com/champions-oncology-expands-integrated-radiopharmaceutical-development-platform-with-in-house-spect-ct-imaging. That release is the growth-side reading of the same commitment, which is why my band crosses zero.

evidence.text: The 'cash halved to $4.9m' fear that dominated the July 27 reaction is likely to be relieved rather than confirmed tonight: fiscal Q1 is Champions' collection quarter - operating cash flow was +$600k in Q1 FY2026 and +$311k in Q1 FY2025, with cash rising from $9.785m to $10.325m in the year-ago Q1 as receivables fell $1.7m - and the company enters this Q1 with its largest-ever year-end receivable, $13.178m, up $1.97m year over year.
evidence.why_not_priced: This requires joining two documents nobody joins on a $49k-a-day name: the FY26 10-K balance sheet (AR $13.178m, cash $4.872m) and the prior-year Q1 10-Q cash-flow statement (Q1 is seasonally cash-generative). Every piece of secondary coverage of the July print stopped at 'ended the year with $4.9 million in cash and no debt' and extrapolated the FY26 burn of $4.5m linearly. If the seasonality were priced there would be no runway framing in the post-print write-ups, and the 10-K's own 'adequate to fund operations through at least August 2027' language would be quoted rather than the cash figure.
evidence.independence: Different source, same direction: the FY26 balance sheet also shows accounts payable stretched to $6.903m from $4.248m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/771856/000162828026049834/R3.htm (2026-07-27). That cuts both ways honestly: it means the AP lever is spent, but it also means the April 30 cash figure was not flattered by it running the other way.

evidence.text: Charles River, whose DSA segment is the closest listed read on preclinical oncology outsourcing demand, said on August 5, 2026 - nine days after Champions last spoke - that it recorded 'the highest net book-to-bill in nearly four years' with improvement 'broad based across our global biopharmaceutical and small and mid-sized biotechnology clients', and raised 2026 organic revenue guidance from -1.5%/-0.5% to 0.0%/+1.0%; that bookings window is precisely Champions' May-July 2026 quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: CRL's own print was covered everywhere and moved CRL; the read-across to a 13.9m-share, 9,450-share-a-day microcap with no analyst coverage is aggregated nowhere. CSBR did not move on August 5. The specific mechanism - Champions' deferred revenue is upfront billings on new bookings, so a bookings recovery in the May-July window would show as a deferred-revenue rebound off the $8.828m multi-year low on tonight's balance sheet - has not been written anywhere I can find. If it were priced you would expect the 20-day run-up to be more than +5.2% on essentially no volume.
evidence.independence: none - I could not find a second CRO or a Champions-specific bookings datum covering the May-July 2026 window, and this is a read-across from a differently-mixed business (CRL's strength is regulated safety assessment, which is later-stage than Champions' TOS discovery work), which is why I have sized it small.

evidence.text: Adobe must guide Q4 net-new Digital Media ARR on this call with the president of the Creativity & Productivity business (David Wadhwani) having resigned effective 2026-09-27 with no named successor in the 8-K, an interim CFO (Steve Day) since June, and a CEO-elect from the enterprise/Digital Experience side who does not take office until 2026-12-01 - i.e. every person who owns or will own that number is either leaving or not yet in post.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market priced the headline - ADBE fell ~7% on 2026-09-04 on the succession and Wadhwani's LinkedIn post, and the 5-day run-up is -9.98%. What it priced was 'we lost a CEO candidate', a governance event. The mechanical consequence is different and is not in any preview I found: the Q4 ARR bar is being set by an interim CFO and an outgoing CEO three weeks before the segment head walks and twelve weeks before a new CEO arrives, which is the textbook set-up for a de-risked guide rather than the 'beat-and-raise minimum' the previews say is required. If this were priced the 25-delta skew would not be -15.2 vol points (the most call-bid name in today's universe) and the preview copy would be arguing about who guides the number rather than about generative AI.
evidence.independence: The CEO appointment itself is independently reported by CNBC, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/03/adobe-anil-chakravarthy-ceo.html (2026-09-03); the interim-CFO leg is independently sourced to the June departure of Dan Durn, https://www.cfodive.com/news/adobe-cfo-leadership-gap-marvell-amid-ceo-search-ai/822849/. Note this finding and finding 2 both predict a soft Q4 ARR guide by different mechanisms and different documents - if the guide is fine, both are wrong together.

evidence.text: On 2026-08-06, three weeks before Adobe's Q3 closed (2026-08-28), Adobe shipped 'Adobe for ChatGPT' - 70+ tools spanning Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, Lightroom, Acrobat and Express, usable 'immediately as a guest' with no Creative Cloud subscription - which lands almost entirely in the Q4 guidance window rather than in the reported Q3 quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: The launch was covered as a distribution win (Engadget, Seeking Alpha) and the sell-side downgrades that set the bear case pre-date it - Morgan Stanley on 2026-07-21 to Underweight with a $240 target. Nobody has tied it to management's own Q2 framing that Q3 ARR would be 'soft by design as traffic rerouting takes hold', which is exactly what free guest access to the paid app stack for ChatGPT's user base is. The Q3 number was pre-excused; the Q4 guide is where an Aug-6 free-funnel expansion actually shows up, and it is guided cold on this call. If the market had focused on it, the consumer-press framing ('stop giving $55 a month to Adobe') would appear in the previews, and the previews are still arguing generic AI disruption instead.
evidence.independence: Independently confirmed and framed as subscription-cannibalising by Windows Central, https://www.windowscentral.com/artificial-intelligence/openai-chatgpt/chatgpt-users-can-now-use-photoshop-for-free-in-the-ai-bot, and by Engadget, https://www.engadget.com/2231088/adobe-new-chatgpt-plugin-brings-70-of-its-tools-to-openai-chatbot/. Shares an outcome (weak Q4 ARR guide) with finding 1 but no document and no mechanism - see the note there.

evidence.text: Figma - the single company the Adobe bear case leans on hardest - guided Q3 2026 revenue to $373.0-375.0m against Q2 actual $370.1m, i.e. 0.8-1.3% sequential growth and ~36% y/y against 48% y/y just delivered, a 12-point one-quarter deceleration guided by the competitor itself.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Figma print was read entirely through its headline - '48% growth, third consecutive quarter of acceleration' - and cited that way in the Adobe share-loss narrative. The sequential arithmetic in the same release points the other way and I found no Adobe preview that does it. If the market had done it, the Adobe bear notes issued after 2026-08-05 would be arguing about whether Figma's seat expansion is topping out rather than treating its acceleration as evidence. Small, because it is a guide from a company two quarters public and everyone discounts those, and because Figma's absolute size is not what determines Adobe's ARR.
evidence.independence: Figma's own investor page carries the same numbers, https://investor.figma.com/news-events/news/news-details/2026/Figma-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx; separately, Salesforce's 2026-08-26 Q2 FY27 print (cRPO +14%, FY guide raised, stock +18%) says enterprise software demand in the Jun-Aug window did not deteriorate, https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2026/08/26/fy27-q2-earnings/.

evidence.text: Insider activity: no Form 4 at all since 2026-08-17 despite the stock falling ~10% in five days and hitting near 52-week lows - no buy cluster, no sell cluster. The only 144 since (2026-09-08) is departed CFO Dan Durn, routine.
Activist involvement - nothing on Elliott, Starboard or ValueAct in ADBE; no 13D on file and the 13G/13G-A stream is routine passive.

WARN / restructuring: no Cal-WARN filing, no restructuring charge in the Q2 10-Q, no 8-K. The 'Adobe layoffs 2026' pages that surface are staffing-agency SEO with no primary source, so I dropped the angle rather than cite it.

FX tailwind to ending ARR: EUR/USD sat ~1.16 through August with a three-month high of 1.1710 on 2026-08-20, i.e. roughly flat across the fiscal quarter versus the 2026-06-11 guide - no mechanical translation surprise to size.

Balance-sheet / disclosure tells in the Q2 10-Q: RPO $22.27bn +13% y/y (in line with revenue +13%), deferred revenue $7.25bn, no new risk-factor language, no ASR, $26.78bn buyback authorisation remaining - nothing anomalous.

Adobe pricing pages and generative-credit terms for a Q3 list-price or credit-enforcement change: the only sources with specific 2026 numbers are SEO aggregators contradicting each other, and helpx returned 403. No primary-source pricing event I would rest a size on.
Adobe community forums / Firefly credit backlash - no concentrated Q3 complaint thread that would read as churn.
Semrush: closed 2026-04-28 at $1.9bn / ~$455m ARR, already in the Q2 base at ~$480m and already publicly identified as the reason the 10.2% FY26 ARR target only looks 'maintained'. Priced.
The stock's own base rate: 'down 10 of the last 12 prints' is already the headline of the Benzinga Q3 preview, so it is wire copy, not an edge.

evidence.text: Kroger bought back only $198m of stock (3m shares) in Q1 2026 against a $2.0bn authorization it says in the same 10-Q it 'expects to complete by the end of fiscal 2026' — a 10%-of-plan pace — while the reaffirmed FY guide of $5.10-$5.30 needs H2 EPS of $2.48-$2.68 against $2.32 last year (+7% to +16%) with the y/y share-count tailwind decaying from -7.4% in Q1 (615m vs 664m diluted) toward ~-3% by Q4 as the FY2025 ASR laps out.
evidence.why_not_priced: The buyback line was never raised on the Q1 call (the transcript contains no management discussion of repurchases at all) and no wire preview mentions it; the previews are anchored on the $1.05 consensus, which management itself pre-guided ('adjusted EPS in line with last year in the second quarter'), so the consensus number carries zero information and the real question — whether the FY range survives an H1 in which adjusted FIFO operating profit grew 1.7% (Q1 $1,544m vs $1,518m) and Q2 EPS is guided flat on a ~6% smaller share count, i.e. adjusted net earnings down ~6% — is not in the coverage. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not be -2.76 vol points with calls bid into a guidance-setting print; a market expecting the FY range to be cut pays for puts.
evidence.independence: Two documents from the same issuer support one finding and the scorer should treat them as one cluster: the Q1 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926075395/tm2618219d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-06-18, Q1 adj FIFO OP $1,544m vs $1,518m, 615m vs 664m diluted, guidance reaffirmed) and the FY2025 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926023800/tm267907d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-03-05, FY2025 adj EPS $4.85, adj FIFO OP $4.9bn, 655m avg diluted, FY2026 guide incl. ~130bp IRA headwind). Genuinely independent corroboration that H2 is the swing factor: Kroger separately committed $1.25bn of cash to the Giant Eagle acquisition on 2026-07-01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926079552/tm2619434d1_8k.htm.

evidence.text: Greg Foran (CEO since 2026-02-09, ex-Walmart U.S. CEO) has his hand-picked operating team landing in the two weeks straddling this print: Nate Faust as EVP/Chief eCommerce Officer effective 2026-09-01 (announced 08-11) and Mark Ibbotson as EVP/Chief Store Operations Officer effective 2026-09-14 (8-K filed 09-02, three days before the quiet period, on a $1m salary plus $3.5m of sign-on equity), both ex-Walmart/Asda.
evidence.why_not_priced: A $1m-salary EVP appointment in a routine item-5.02 8-K nine days before a print draws no wire coverage and no analyst note — I found no sell-side commentary linking it to the quarter. The mechanism the market is missing is timing, not the person: Foran's documented Walmart playbook is price investment funded by cost-out with near-term margin sacrifice, he has already said publicly he will cut prices broadly and double new-store openings to 70-80 next year, and a CEO does not import a Chief Store Operations Officer to keep executing an inherited plan. Guidance resets are overwhelmingly delivered once the new team is seated. If the market had focused on this, the print would carry a visible 'reset risk' premium in put skew rather than the -2.76 call-bid skew actually quoted.
evidence.independence: Separate source, separate document: Kroger's own release naming Faust, https://ir.kroger.com/news/news-details/2026/Kroger-names-Nate-Faust-Executive-Vice-President-and-Chief-eCommerce-Officer/default.aspx (2026-08-11). Foran's appointment and Walmart record: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926012061/tm265602d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-02-09). This rests on different documents from finding 1 and a different mechanism (management intent vs arithmetic), but both point at the same event — a Q2 guidance reset — so a scorer should not read them as two independent probabilities of that event.

evidence.text: The two peer prints that actually overlap Kroger's Q2 window (2026-05-24 to 2026-08-15) show the traffic going to mass and club, not to conventional supermarkets: Walmart U.S. comped +2.6% for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 led by transactions and RAISED FY27 guidance, and Costco's U.S. comp ex-gasoline and FX was +5.6% for the four weeks ended 2026-08-30 — against Kroger's own guide of identical sales 'roughly in line with the first quarter' at 1.0%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The read-across note the street actually wrote was on 2026-07-23, off Albertsons' guidance cut, and Albertsons' quarter ended 2026-06-20 — it covers only the first four weeks of Kroger's Q2 and says nothing about July or August. Walmart's May-July quarter and Costco's August month are the only public reads on the back two-thirds of Kroger's quarter, and nobody re-ran the read-across on them because Walmart's print was framed as a Walmart story (tariff refunds, e-commerce, guidance raise). The distinction matters directionally: a soft-industry quarter is forgivable and a share-loss quarter is not, and share loss is what forces a price-investment reset. Had this been priced, Kroger would not be flat (+1.5%) over 20 days while Walmart raised guidance in the middle of that window.
evidence.independence: Costco, a different company and filing: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-August-Sales-Results/default.aspx (released 2026-09-02, four weeks ended 2026-08-30). Also, Ahold Delhaize's U.S. comp ex-gasoline was only +0.8% for its Q2, with the drags quantified as -0.9pp SNAP and egg deflation and -0.7pp IRA pharmacy pricing: https://newsroom.aholddelhaize.com/ahold-delhaize-reports-resilient-q2-2026-results-and-reiterates-guidance-for-the-year/ (2026-08-05) — i.e. conventional U.S. supermarkets ran near zero in the same window Walmart ran +2.6%.

evidence.text: Grocery dollar inflation is running materially hotter in Kroger's Q2 window than in the Q1 window that management extrapolated from: food-at-home CPI was +1.9% y/y in March 2026 but +2.7% y/y in each of May, June and July 2026, so Kroger's 'roughly in line with the first quarter' 1.0% identical-sales guide, set on 2026-06-18, embeds roughly 50-60bp less price than the quarter is actually carrying.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the one leg that cuts upward and it is the reason the answer is -2.3 and not -4. It is public and free, but the previews all quote the EPS consensus rather than the comp, and Kroger's identical-sales line is the number this stock trades on. Management guided the comp on 2026-06-18 with only March and April CPI in hand; June and July food-at-home prints (both +2.7%) landed after. Two of the eight prints in the reaction history were up 5%+ on a comp beat, so a 150-160bp comp against a 100bp guide is a real upside path that the -2.76 call-bid skew is arguably already leaning toward — which is exactly why I am sizing it as a partial offset rather than the headline.
evidence.independence: USDA ERS confirms the July figure independently of the BLS TED article: 'food-at-home CPI was unchanged from June 2026 to July 2026 and 2.7 percent higher than in July 2025', https://ers.usda.gov/data-products/food-price-outlook/summary-findings. Corroborating that the price is showing up at conventional supermarket registers: Weis Markets comped +2.3% for the 13 weeks ended 2026-06-27 despite a ~$18.2m IRA pharmacy revenue drag, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000105418/000010541826000048/wmk-20260804xex99d1.htm (2026-08-04).

evidence.text: Form 4 cluster of 13 filings on 2026-07-14/16 — read two of them, they are code-F tax withholding on restricted stock vesting (e.g. Carin Fike, 56 shares at $56.56); only one genuine open-market sale (Yael Cosset, 30,000 shares for $1.764m on 07-14), not a signal
UFCW labour action — the King Soopers/Local 7 strike material is all February 2025 and the SoCal tentative agreements are 2025; found no 2026 strike or contract expiry inside or after the quarter
Kroger layoffs/store closures — the '1,000 corporate layoffs' and '60 store closures' stories date to August 2025 under interim CEO Ron Sargent, relabelled by search as 2026; discarded on date

SNAP as a fresh negative — national participation fell to 36.6m in May 2026 from 42.2m in May 2025 (foodtradenews 2026-08-27), but May 2026 is inside Kroger's Q1, so the y/y drag is already in the +1.0% Q1 comp and in the reaffirmed guide; management named it on the Q1 call ('most impacted across three states'). Not incremental.

IRA Medicare maximum-fair-price pharmacy headwind — real and quantified at peers (Ahold -0.7pp, Weis ~$18.2m, Walmart -80bp), but Kroger disclosed ~130bp of it inside FY2026 guidance in the 2026-03-05 release, so it is explicitly priced
Giant Eagle antitrust/deal risk — announced 2026-07-01, closes 2027, fully covered; leverage at 1.75x vs a 2.3-2.5x target means the $1.25bn cash does not force a buyback trade-off
Kroger IR news-release index page and the Q4 2025 IR permalink both returned HTTP 404; used the SEC 8-K exhibits instead
Searched for a Kroger-specific operational event in the quarter (outage, recall, cyber, pricing-page or membership change) and found nothing dated inside 2026-05-24 to 2026-08-15

evidence.text: IAA/RB Global reported automotive unit volume of 658,800 lots, +11% year-over-year for Apr-Jun 2026 — two of the three months in Copart's fiscal Q4 — calling it the 'sixth consecutive quarter of outperforming the broader market,' with the CFO stating 'unit volume growth was supported by continued net market share gains, while broader industry volumes remain under pressure'; against a flat industry that arithmetic implies Copart's US insurance units were down roughly 5-7% in the quarter it is about to report, worse than the -4.2% it posted for Feb-Apr.
evidence.why_not_priced: Copart's entire 20-day run-up window opens AFTER RB Global's 2026-08-04 print, and on 2026-09-03 the stock rose 4% on a JPMorgan upgrade whose stated thesis was that Copart 'appears to be picking up share in some states from an insurer' — the literal inverse of what the competitor reported for the same months. If the market had weighted IAA's own disclosed number you would see the 25-delta skew positive rather than -2.33, put/call open interest above rather than 0.71, and no 4% upgrade day into a name that has fallen after six of its last seven prints. The competitive story in the wire is generic ('IAA pressure'); the unpriced part is that the specific quarter being reported is one in which the competitor has already published its side of the ledger.
evidence.independence: Copart's own last disclosure points the same way from a different document: Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-04-30) global insurance units -2.7% and US insurance units -4.2%, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260521385731/en/Copart-Reports-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Financial-Results (2026-05-21). Note the offset inside my own primary source, which is why the band reaches +0.5: the same RB Global transcript reports total-loss frequency up 90bp to a record 23.3% with 'leading indicators of the total loss frequency have improved modestly in recent months' — an industry tailwind for Copart assignments that I have deliberately not filed as a separate finding because it rests on the same document.

evidence.text: Copart is in a live, reported process to acquire CCC Intelligent Solutions (~$4.2bn equity value plus net debt), it upsized its revolver on 2026-01-23 to $1.25bn with a $500m incremental option explicitly permitting acquisitions, and on 2026-08-13 it seated David J. Berger — Wilson Sonsini's senior M&A-litigation and shareholder-activism partner — on the board, announced 2026-08-17, one day before the Bloomberg leak; the earnings call is a natural venue for a deal that would consume essentially all of the $4.2bn cash the current holder base owns this stock for.
evidence.why_not_priced: CPRT rose across the window in which the CCC report broke, so the market is treating a possible $5bn+ cash-and-debt acquisition as free strategic optionality rather than as balance-sheet consumption. If it were pricing deal risk you would see puts bid into the print; instead the 25-delta skew is -2.33 with calls paid. evidence.text: RF Industries added brand-new deferred-tax-asset release language to its Q2 FY2026 10-Q MD&A that is absent from the Q1 10-Q filed three months earlier — 'it is reasonably possible that a reduction of a significant portion of the valuation allowance may be appropriate in a future reporting period', with 'cumulative losses' recast into the past tense ('In prior periods, the Company recorded a valuation allowance due primarily to cumulative losses') — against a $4,521,000 allowance which on 11,424,572 diluted shares is roughly $0.40 per share of potential one-time GAAP EPS, versus a $0.18 two-analyst consensus.
evidence.why_not_priced: This lives in the MD&A of a $110m microcap's 10-Q, not in the release, not in the 8-K exhibit and not on the call — and the comparison that makes it a signal requires pulling the prior quarter's 10-Q and diffing the tax paragraph. If it were priced there would be at least one sell-side or newswire note framing the Q3 print as a possible valuation-allowance quarter, and with only two analysts covering the name there is none; the consensus is a single clean $0.18 with no reconciliation between a GAAP and an ex-tax number, which is what you would not see if anyone had modelled a $0.40/share non-cash credit. The 'reasonably possible / future reporting period' construction is the standard ASC 740 pre-announcement companies file one to four quarters before they act, and Q3 (ended 31 July 2026) would be the fifth consecutive profitable quarter.
evidence.independence: None that is genuinely independent — the finding IS the diff between two of the company's own filings, the Q1 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/740664/000143774926008410/rfil20260131_10q.htm (allowance $4,538,000, no release language, negative evidence still stated in the present tense). The 11,424,572 diluted share count used for the per-share arithmetic is from the Q2 8-K earnings exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/740664/000143774926020657/ex_975747.htm, filed the same day, so treat all three as one source cluster. Weight of timing risk is real: the fiscal-year-end (31 October) assessment is the more conventional moment to act, so the low end of my band is a Q3 that merely repeats the language.

evidence.why_not_priced: The sweep's own brief treats the -22.5% 20-day drawdown as the single most specific question on this name, which is how most participants will read it too: a halving into a confirmed date reads as the market discounting a bad quarter or an imminent raise. The filing record says the opposite — a $110m company that had actually lost a customer, drawn on a shelf, or seen management sell would normally leave a trace on EDGAR, and there is none. If the market were pricing a dilution risk you would expect at least an active S-3 takedown or a borrow build; if it were pricing a fundamental break you would expect an 8-K or a withdrawn guide. evidence.text: COMEX copper ran at or near all-time highs through the whole of RF Industries' fiscal Q3 (1 May - 31 July 2026), printing a record $6.83/lb in August and sitting at $6.47/lb on 11 September, +41.2% over twelve months — against a business where custom cabling (37% of H1 FY2026 sales) plus interconnect (35%) is 72% of revenue and where the bar management set is a record 35.1% gross margin it called sustainable above $20m of quarterly revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: Two analysts cover this name and the margin line they are modelling is the 35.1% management guided to as sustainable; nobody builds a copper pass-through lag into a $110m connector assembler. If input cost were in the price you would see a sell-side margin cut or at least a preview flagging it, and the only rating action in the window was a generic Zacks strong-buy-to-hold on 22 August. The mechanism is small but one-directional: RFIL buys finished cable, so a rising copper input shows up with a one-to-two-quarter lag precisely in the quarter being reported, and at roughly 15-25% of cabling COGS a 10% input move is worth about a point of gross margin, or ~$0.02 of EPS against a $0.18 bar.
evidence.independence: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/14/copper-trump-tariffs-metal-commodities-trade-war.html (URL path confirms 2026-08-14) independently documents the record COMEX level and the Section 232 tariff overhang. Honest caveat: Q2 FY2026 (Feb-Apr) already carried copper near records and still printed 35.1%, so the quarter-over-quarter delta is not something I could establish, which is why the band is wide and the point estimate small.

evidence.text: CoinShares' own US ETF (BRRR) 10-Q puts bitcoin at $58,391 on 30 June 2026 vs $87,650 on 31 Dec 2025 (-33.4%) and BRRR net assets down 32.3% despite net creations, so group gross AUM of $7.4bn at FY2025 falls to roughly $5bn at 30 June; at the disclosed blended 170bp yield that is ~$50m of H1 asset-management revenue against $126.4m for FY2025, i.e. an annualised run-rate that turns the 3.0x trailing P/E screeners still display on CSHR into roughly 12x.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no consensus to be surprised against: the only visible sell-side coverage is a single KBW initiation (Outperform, PT cut $9 to $7), and CoinShares has published no interim P&L covering any part of 2026 - the last hard number on the tape is the 1 May 2026 FY2025 release headlined 'Reflecting Continued Strong Growth'. If the earnings-power reset were priced, the stock would not still be carried at a 3.04 P/E and a 7.66% indicated yield on the retail data pages that most of a 202k-ADV de-SPAC's marginal buyers read, and the 20-day run-up would not be +5.0%.
evidence.independence: The FY2025 release itself gives the $7.4bn AUM, $126.4m asset-management revenue and ~170bp blended yield used to convert the AUM decline into revenue: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2087587/000121390026050703/ea028870801ex99-1.htm (6-K, 2026-05-01). Note this same FY2025 document is also the source of the segment figures in finding 2 - treat the two as one source cluster on that document, with the BRRR 10-Q the independent leg here.

evidence.text: Capital Markets - 37% of FY2025 revenue and gains ($73.1m) but 44% of segment EBITDA ($57.7m of $131.3m) - is the one line that cannot be reconstructed from the monthly AUM CoinShares publishes, and its largest single component was disclosed as ETH staking at $4.3m in Q2 2025 alone, a line that scales with token price and with a futures basis that compressed through a half in which industry ETP AUM fell from ~$160bn in May to ~$141bn by 1 June on record outflows.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sweep's own cheap read is that H1 fee revenue is reconstructable from published fund-flow data; that is exactly why the market will anchor on AUM and mis-size the half. A US investor modelling CSHR as an asset manager applies a fee rate to AUM and gets the smaller, more resilient half of segment EBITDA right and the larger, regime-dependent half wrong. If this were understood, the name would not be quoted on a trailing P/E at all and the 63% realised vol would already have an option chain around it rather than 368 total open interest.
evidence.independence: The segment split it rests on comes from the FY2025 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2087587/000121390026050703/ea028870801ex99-1.htm, 2026-05-01), which is shared with finding 1; the Q2 2025 release and the fund-flow volume (https://researchblog.coinshares.com/volume-288-digital-asset-fund-flows-weekly-report-166b82513893, 2026-06-01) are the independent legs.

evidence.text: The lock-up agreed at listing expires 1 October 2026 - 12 trading days after this print - and the day after the print shareholders vote on a 2026 Equity Incentive Plan with an 11% initial pool plus up to 3% a year for 2027-2029 (up to ~20% of the 131.8m shares outstanding), while a co-founder/director's 10b5-1 plan starts selling in September and adds 1.5m shares of monthly diversification sales the moment the lock-up lifts.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 1 October lock-up date appears nowhere in the wire copy on the print; it is a clause inside a trading-plan press release, and no earnings preview or calendar row carries it. The headline 11% pool has been on the tape since 24 August, but the configuration - last information event before the entire pre-deal register can sell, with a dilution vote wedged between the two - is a sequencing fact rather than a headline, and it caps the upside to any good print because holders who want out have 12 sessions to act. If the market had focused on it, CSHR would not have rallied 2.84% on the EGM notice day.
evidence.independence: The EGM resolutions (25% buyback authority at $0.01-$20.00, 11% pool, 3% evergreen 2027-2029, 131.8m shares outstanding, record date 27 August) are a separate document: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CSHR/notice-of-virtual-extraordinary-general-meeting-of-coin-shares-plc-60dgtz7l5wya.html (2026-08-24), filed as a 6-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002087587/000121390026092804/ea0303148-6k_coinshares.htm.

evidence.text: Bitcoin is ~$78,800 on 8-10 September against the $58,391 close on 30 June that this release will report AUM at - a 35% recovery after the balance-sheet date - and the EGM the next morning asks for authority to buy back up to 25% of shares at $0.01-$20.00, giving management both a strong current-AUM update and a live capital-return lever to pair with a weak historical half.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced - the BTC chart is public and is most of why the 20-day run-up is +5.0% against a -10.7% five-day - which is why this is sized small and positive rather than large. What is not priced is that management chose to report the day before a vote it needs to win, which is the maximum-incentive configuration for pairing a weak H1 with a current-quarter AUM print and buyback language; nothing in the coverage of the 30 July 'confirms quarterly reporting cadence' release anticipates a buyback being signalled at the results rather than after the vote.
evidence.independence: The 30 July release frames the EGM as buyback-flexibility driven and is a separate document: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/30/3335872/0/en/CoinShares-Confirms-Quarterly-Reporting-Cadence-Seeks-Shareholder-Approval-for-Buyback-Authority.html (2026-07-30). The 30 June bitcoin level comes from the BRRR 10-Q used in finding 1 - same source cluster for that leg.

evidence.text: Richard Nash has signed as 'Interim Chief Financial Officer' since the 20-F certification dated 30 April 2026 and is still 'Interim CFO' in the 8 September results notice - over five months with no permanent CFO named - while the company's own governance page lists him without the qualifier, and CoinShares issued no press release at all between 1 May and 21 July 2026 before publishing a release whose purpose was to confirm it would report quarterly.
evidence.why_not_priced: A company does not put out a release confirming it intends to report quarterly unless it has been asked why it went quiet; that release, an eleven-week communications gap, and an interim finance chief presenting the issuer's first ever SEC-format interim accounts together raise the chance of a presentation the market cannot reconcile to the Swedish-era numbers. If this were priced there would be a permanent-CFO search story in the coverage and the governance page and the press releases would not disagree on the man's title.

evidence.text: The Nasdaq minimum-bid 180-day compliance date is 2026-09-21 — five business days after this print — and the cure the company itself named in the 8-K ('propose a reverse stock split to shareholders at its 2026 annual meeting') cannot complete in time, because Hain's annual meeting is held in early November (the 2025 meeting's item 5.07 8-K was filed 2025-11-05) and no PRE 14A or DEF 14A has been filed as of today; the only listing outcomes actually available in the week of the print are a transfer down to the Nasdaq Capital Market for a second 180 days, or a delisting determination.

evidence.text: The binding financial covenant is the 2.00:1.00 minimum interest coverage ratio, not the 5.50:1.00 maximum net secured leverage ratio the CFO points to ('leverage of 4.3x... plenty of headroom under the covenant of 5.5x'): interest and other financing expense ROSE to $45.1m for the nine months to 2026-03-31 from $38.4m a year earlier despite a $101m term-loan paydown, because the September 2025 Fourth Amendment raised the Term SOFR margin from 3.00% to 4.00%, while the TTM adjusted EBITDA implied by the company's own disclosed ratios fell from about $138m at 2025-06-30 to about $118m at 2026-03-31 — putting coverage near 2.0-2.3x against a 2.00x floor at the June 2026 test date being reported on Monday.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every public discussion of this credit agreement — the Q3 call, the coverage of it, the FY2025 release — quotes only the leverage test, which has 1.2 turns of headroom and looks comfortable; the coverage test added and reset by the Fourth Amendment is quoted nowhere. If the market had done this arithmetic, the interest-expense line rising year-on-year through a deleveraging would be the headline of every preview rather than the $155m of debt reduction. I flag the honest weakness: the covenant almost certainly tests Consolidated CASH Interest Expense, which excludes deferred-financing-fee amortisation that is large after two amendments, so true headroom could be a full turn wider — hence the wide band and the +1 upside bound.
evidence.independence: The 5.50x leverage level and the 2.00x coverage level are confirmed from a DIFFERENT document, the company's FY2025 results release of 2025-09-15 and the Fourth Amendment description therein — https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/15/3149840/0/en/Hain-Celestial-Reports-Fiscal-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2025-Financial-Results.html — and the 100bp margin step-up from the amendment exhibit itself, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910406/000119312525203534/hain-ex10_1-5.htm. NOTE: the EBITDA implication and the $45.1m interest figure both come from the same Q3 FY26 10-Q as the primary source, so treat that part as one document, not two.

evidence.text: The -20.65% five-day run-in has no informational cause I could locate: no 8-K of any item since 2026-05-11, no company press release since 2026-08-17, and HAIN is NOT among the ten S&P SmallCap 600 deletions announced 2026-09-04 effective 2026-09-21 — so the de-rate into the print is positioning and forced supply, not news, in a stock last reported 13.9% short.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the inverse case — it says part of what IS in the price is not information. The baseline shows 20-day run-up at only -0.82% against -20.65% over five days, i.e. the stock round-tripped a rally inside three weeks with no filing and no release to explain either leg. evidence.text: NOAA's summer summary, published three trading days before this print, makes June-August 2026 the warmest summer for the contiguous US in the 132-year record (74.4F, +3.0F above average) with August 2026 the warmest August ever recorded (75.6F, daytime max 88.6F) - June and July sit inside D&B's fiscal Q2 (May 6 - Aug 4) and August sits in the Q3 quarter-to-date that management will be asked about on the call, and air-conditioned eatertainment is the category that gains share from record heat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Weather is not an aggregated financial datum - there is no estimate-revision line, no Zacks field and no wire item that carries it into a Q2 model. NOAA's release landed 2026-09-09/10 (CNN's URL path /2026/09/09/ dates it independently) and PLAY spent that window making a new 52-week low: if the market had connected a 132-year demand record to the quarter being reported, the 25-delta skew would not be +6.18 with downside bid and the stock would not be 18.35% lower over 20 days.
