evidence.text: High Tide carries a C$57.9m derivative liability for the put option over the 49% of Remexian it does not own, priced at 3.64065x Remexian's trailing annual EBITDA and valued by Monte Carlo with 82% annualised EBITDA volatility and a 15% IRR — so the liability ratchets up mechanically with exactly the record German quarter (10+ tonnes, +33% sequential) the company pre-announced, and the remeasurement lands below the three metrics the pre-announcement quantified.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Aug 4 pre-announcement quantified revenue, gross profit and adjusted EBITDA — the three measures that all exclude this item — and every wire story and preview ran on those three. The liability moved C$20.9m in its first two-month stub period in FY2025 against a Q2 FY2026 reported net income of C$24k, so a remeasurement of even a few million flips the reported bottom line to a loss against a quarter the company has already called a record. If the market had priced the mechanic, the Aug 4 release of record German tonnage would not have been a clean +4.65% up day, and the sell-side average target would not sit at $4.67 against a $2.57 spot with the put equal to roughly 19% of the US$221m market cap and settleable in cash or shares at High Tide's discretion from 2027-09-02.
evidence.independence: The put's economics (3.64065x TTM adjusted EBITDA, cash-or-shares at High Tide's discretion, 5-year term after 24 months) are independently described in the deal announcement — https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/high-tide-closes-acquisition-of-a-majority-stake-in-remexian-pharma-gmbh-302543298.html (2025-09-02). evidence.text: The German MedCanG amendment that would ban mail-order dispensing and require in-person consultation before a first cannabis prescription was NOT voted before the 2026 summer recess and remains stuck in the Bundestag health committee over an unresolved coalition split on the scope of the mail-order ban, with a vote realistically no earlier than September 2026 and implementation drifting to late autumn/winter 2026.
evidence.source_date: 2026-09 (page states the bill was not called before the summer recess 2026 and remains in the Gesundheitsausschuss; vote expected 'from September 2026 at the earliest')
evidence.why_not_priced: English-language cannabis coverage last framed this as 'Germany advances MedCanG amendments' and readers carried a spring-2026 enactment as the base case; the granular status — which committee, which coalition disagreement, which reading has not happened — exists only in German-language legal and trade sources. Remexian is a pharmacy wholesaler whose growth is fed by telemedicine-driven mail-order demand, so the delay is a direct extension of the runway that is under-reported in exactly the sources a cannabis analyst reads. If it were priced, the stock would not have traded to $2.15 on 2026-08-03, within 6% of its 52-week low, in the same week it pre-announced a record German quarter.
evidence.independence: The scope of the proposed ban and the spring-2026 expectation it is now slipping from are documented separately at https://www.gleisslutz.com/en/know-how/update-cannabis-legalisation-german-federal-government-prohibit-telemedical-prescriptions-medical-cannabis and the government bill itself is BT-Drs. 21/3061, https://dserver.bundestag.de/btd/21/030/2103061.pdf (2025-12-03).

evidence.text: Free cash flow is the one metric the pre-announcement left out and it was already deteriorating before the German step-up: Q2 FY2026 FCF fell to C$1.5m from C$4.9m a year earlier on working-capital investment, TTM FCF is C$13.4m, cash was C$36.5m against C$68.2m of debt, and the company has publicly committed to staying FCF-positive for fiscal 2026 while Q3 revenue steps up C$16-21m sequentially on receivables-heavy German distribution plus a 20+ store build.

If cash conversion were the market's focus, the C$40m BMO facility closed on 2026-08-05 — of which C$25m refinances a C$6m connectFirst balance and C$15m refinances existing second-lien debentures, so it adds almost no net new headroom against a C$57.9m put falling due from 2027 — would have been read as a liquidity event rather than as the cost-of-capital win the headline sold.

evidence.text: BIOX's Nasdaq 180-day minimum-bid-price compliance period expires TODAY, 2026-09-14 - the same session the FY26 results are due - and at $0.4350 compliance is arithmetically impossible, so within days the company must disclose either a transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market with a written commitment to cure (in practice a reverse split) or a Staff delisting determination; it has no shareholder authority for a split, its 2026-01-30 AGM agenda carried only FY2025 accounts, four directors and the auditor, and no EGM has been noticed.
evidence.why_not_priced: A known, dated, binary listing deadline should leave fingerprints and leaves none: run_up_20d is -4.05% and run_up_5d -0.74% (no drift into the date), short interest is 913,482 shares = 2.03% of float as of 2026-09-09, and the entire option chain is 2,023 contracts of open interest with a put/call OI ratio of 0.01 and no two-sided ATM market. Nobody has bought a put, shorted a share, or sold into it. If the market had focused on this you would see a bid for downside protection and a visible pre-deadline slide, as sub-$1 names routinely show in the fortnight before a compliance expiry. I checked the eligibility arithmetic myself rather than assuming the worst: total equity was $95.7m and MVPHS is roughly $18-24m, so BIOX does clear the Nasdaq Capital Market Equity Standard ($5m equity, $15m MVPHS) and a second 180 days is genuinely available - which is why the band runs positive at the top. If the market had priced the reversal the three-estimate EPS would not be a token penny while revenue was revised toward the top of the company's own range, and the 20-day run-up would not be -0.92% with WTI up from $79 in July to $97 in September. This name demonstrably trades the GAAP derivative line rather than looking through it: the only double-digit reaction in its seven-print history was the quarter the mark went the other way.
evidence.independence: WTI settlement levels are from an independent source (FRED DCOILWTICO: $102.86 on 2026-03-31, $70.56 on 2026-06-30, $97.26 on 2026-09-09) — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO ; the hedge strikes and the $6.26m net liability are from the 10-Q, a different document from the 424B5 that finding 2 rests on.

evidence.text: The 2026-08-19 prospectus supplement discloses that at 6/30/2026 EPM had cash of $6.1m and credit-facility borrowings of $56.5m — debt unchanged from 3/31/2026 while cash rose from $2.6m — meaning the June quarter generated roughly $7.8m after paying the $4.26m quarterly dividend, comfortably the best coverage quarter of FY2026 for a stock yielding 12.7% whose entire equity story is the 52-quarter dividend streak.
evidence.why_not_priced: These figures appear only in a prospectus supplement; the concurrent 8-K press releases of 08-18 (acquisition) and 08-19 (offering pricing) contain no preliminary results at all, so nothing about the June balance sheet ever reached a wire. Nine months to 3/31/26 went the other way — $12.6m of dividends paid with cash falling to $2.6m and $56.5m drawn against a $65m borrowing base — which is why the coverage question is what the sell-side notes lead on. If the improvement were priced, the stock would not be 31% below its 52-week high with the dividend declaration on 09-10 passing without a move.
evidence.independence: Corroborated at the 3/31/2026 end by the fiscal Q3 press release (cash $2.6m, debt $56.5m, dividend paid $4,261k) — https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/12/3293500/0/en/evolution-petroleum-reports-fiscal-third-quarter-2026-results-and-declares-0-12-per-share-cash-dividend-for-the-fiscal-fourth-quarter.html . NOTE shared-source caution: the same preliminary paragraph in this 424B5 also brackets FY26 revenue at $84-88m and production at 6,800-7,200 BOEPD, which I deliberately did NOT file as a separate finding because consensus already sits inside both brackets.

evidence.text: The dividend binary the sweep flagged is dead: $0.12 for fiscal Q1 2027 was declared on the wire on 2026-09-10, five days before the print, matching the company's habit of declaring the Q4-cycle dividend separately (it did the same on 2025-09-11). No cut risk survives into the release. https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/10/3360018/0/en/evolution-petroleum-declares-0-12-per-share-cash-dividend-for-fiscal-q1-2027.html

Implied Q4 production: backing 9M actuals (7,315 / 7,380 / 6,700 BOEPD) out of the 424B5 FY range gives a Q4 band of 5,792-7,396 BOEPD, midpoint ~6,594 — but Zacks consensus is already 6,855 BOEPD against 7,198 a year ago, so the third consecutive sequential decline and the unmet 'Louisiana 23 wells / TexMex +100 BOEPD' promises from the May call are inside the estimate. Dropped as priced.

Impairment / reserve writedown risk: the FY2026 SEC price deck (12-month average of first-of-month WTI, Jul-25 to Jun-26) computes to ~$73.2/bbl from FRED, above the FY2025 deck, so a year-end reserve or successful-efforts impairment is unlikely rather than a hidden risk.

Insider activity: the only 2026 Form 4s are quarterly cluster filings by four reporting persons on 2026-07-02 and 2026-09-03 (routine director compensation cadence, same pattern both quarters) — no open-market cluster. https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001006655&type=4

evidence.text: The bearish Chinese-travel datapoint circulating since 2026-08-31 — Flight Master's projection that Chinese carriers' July+August traffic would fall 3.6% y/y to 142m, 'the first contraction in the peak season since 2022' — is contradicted by CAAC's actual July 2026 print published ten days earlier: 74.63m passenger trips, +3.9% y/y, domestic +4.1%, international +2.3%; and forward bookings measured by 2026-09-08 for the unusual 13-day 25 Sep-7 Oct holiday window show 6.06m domestic air tickets (+~14% y/y) and 2.07m international/cross-border (+~7% y/y), with multi-destination trips +25% y/y.
evidence.why_not_priced: The projection, not the print, is what got syndicated: the -3.6% figure ran in the 2026-08-31 wire story about the Big Three's H1 losses and has been the frame for Chinese travel demand ever since, while the CAAC volume release got a Xinhua paragraph and no equity coverage. If the market held the volume picture (air volumes +3.9% in July, Big-3 H1 revenue +9.7%/+11.1%/+10.5% — a cost/fuel problem, not a demand problem) plus double-digit forward holiday ticket growth measured a week ago, TCOM would not be printing a fresh 52-week low on the day of the print (spot 39.535, only 2.16% above the 52-week low) and the 25-delta skew would be negative with calls bid rather than +0.61 vol points with put/call OI at 0.90. All of this post-dates the company's last guidance of 2026-06-24, so none of it is in the +3%-8% Q2 guide the sell side is marking to.
evidence.independence: The same Big-3 H1 results that carried the -3.6% projection also disclose revenue growth of +10.5%/+11.1%/+9.7% with losses driven by a 35-38% fuel cost increase — a different fact in the same document that cuts the opposite way to its own headline: https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2026/08/31/china039s-three-biggest-airlines-post-heavy-first-half-losses-as-fuel-shock-bites . Separately and from a different source, the 25 Sep-7 Oct booking data (Qunar, a Trip.com Group subsidiary, and Umetrip): https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/09/11/chinas-13-day-holiday-hack-sends-travel-bookings-up-119/ (2026-09-11).

evidence.text: China industry hotel RevPAR fell ~6% y/y in July 2026 (occupancy -3pp, ADR -1%) and Hilton cut its full-year China RevPAR outlook from roughly flat to a low-single-digit decline — a rate/ADR deflation that lands on Trip.com's highest-take-rate line, accommodation reservation (RMB6.5bn and +17% y/y in Q1 2026), and that post-dates the 2026-06-24 guidance, so tonight's Q3 outlook is the first management commentary to incorporate it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced and I am sizing it as such — this got a CNBC story and a Goldman note, so it is nearer wire copy than edge. What is not priced is the interaction: OTA accommodation revenue is commission on room-nights x ADR, so a market reading 'Chinese travel volumes are fine' off holiday booking counts is reading the wrong variable, and a Q3 revenue guide at or below the Q2 +3%-8% band is the single most likely thing to move this name — the last guide-down, on 2026-06-24, produced a -12.55% next-day reaction. If this were fully in the price the 25-delta skew would be materially positive rather than +0.61 vol points.
evidence.independence: Tongcheng Travel's own Q2 2026 print (2026-08-26/31, a different company reporting the same market) shows the split: accommodation revenue +11.1% in 1H on ADR growth and a mix shift to 3-star-and-above, while transportation ticketing fell 2.3% — https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/tongcheng-travels-revenue-reaches-rmb9-992-8-million-in-1h2026--302858196.html . Note this cuts partly AGAINST my own finding on ADR, which is why the band is wide and the size small.

evidence.text: Whether the RMB5.301bn SAMR penalty (RMB3,521m fine + RMB1,658m confiscation + RMB122m deposit refund, decision 2026-07-25, 6-K filed 2026-07-27) would be a surprise as to accounting period — it is not: no provision was taken in Q1 (company said it could not estimate losses), but that it lands in the June quarter is already in published previews, e.g. the Seeking Alpha Q2 preview of 2026-09-13 and Bamboo Works. Take-rate/market-share damage from the SAMR remedies (cessation of exclusive cooperation, abolition of 'all-network lowest price', removal of automated pricing tools) — thoroughly covered in the 2026-07-27 fine coverage and named explicitly in the 2026-09-13 preview. Priced.

A new or enlarged buyback as an offsetting announcement — the US$5bn authorisation dates to Aug 2025 and ~US$916m was executed by late April 2026, but I could find no HKEX monthly-return or next-day-disclosure evidence of July/August 2026 repurchase activity, and the company's pattern is to announce capital returns with Q4 results in February, not with Q2. No evidence either way; not filed.

Hong Kong 9961.HK disclosures for anything the ADR tape has not seen — no dividend-consideration language in the 2026-09-02 board announcement (SEC ex-99.2 is a plain scheduling press release, not an HKEX board-meeting notice), and the 2026-06-30 filing is only the AGM results.

A September-dated company-specific surprise: no executive departure, no new regulatory action, no 6-K between 2026-09-02 and today. The co-founder resignations (Min Fan, Qi Ji) were 2026-02-25 and the Hagens Berman securities class action covers 30 Apr 2024 - 13 Jan 2026 — both old and priced.

The reporting-date drift (Q1 2025 reported ~19 May 2025 vs Q1 2026 on 24 Jun 2026; Q2 2025 on 1 Sep 2025 vs Q2 2026 on 15 Sep 2026). Genuinely odd and unexplained in any filing I could find, and H1 results on 16 Sep sits well past the two-month HKEX interim deadline, but I could not establish whether a waiver applies or find any market commentary on it. Unexplained, unsized, not filed.

evidence.text: Charlie's Holdings' shareholder letter of 2026-09-09 - seven days before Ispire's print - says the age-gated launch is still only a 'pilot test ... this fall' and that shipping waits on Ispire's side ('As soon as IKE's software developers complete their final tests of the consumer app, we will begin shipping'), against Ispire CEO Michael Wang telling the 2026-02-06 call that Charlie's would launch 'in the next two to three months' at 'between 2 million chips a month and 3 million chips a month' and 'we should start seeing results in the next quarter' - i.e. exactly the Apr-Jun fiscal Q4 being reported on 09-16.
evidence.why_not_priced: Charlie's is an OTCQB microcap and the letter is a partner-side document that no ISPR wire story references; ISPR's own coverage since March has been the '$50-70 billion flavoured vape TAM' framing with no unit numbers attached. If the market had priced the non-conversion, the posted ISPR consensus for this print would not still be +$0.01 EPS on $21.34m of revenue with a $3.50 mean target against a $1.42 spot - that is a sell-side that has not touched its model since the age-gating narrative began.
evidence.independence: Two other documents point the same way and neither is the letter: Charlie's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (Ispire's fiscal Q4) contains no mention of IKE, IKE Tech, Ispire, age-gating or any related licensing agreement anywhere in the filing - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001134765/000143774926028182/chuc20260630_10q.htm ; and Charlie's Q1 2026 release of 2026-05-20 had already pushed the age-gated disposable launch out to 'Q3 2026' from Ispire's February 'two to three months' - https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CHUC/charlie-s-holdings-reports-first-quarter-2026-82dn9fyj78b4.html . evidence.text: The 'significant development deal around our age-gating technology with a leading global nicotine company in the coming weeks' that Michael Wang promised on the 2026-02-06 call has not been announced in the seven months since: Ispire's own press-release index runs 2026-02-04 to 2026-08-17 with nothing of the kind (the only deal in the gap is the Jincheng Pharma nicotine-pouch JV, a Chinese pharma manufacturing tie-up, not an age-gating licence), and the 2026-05-07 Q3 call did not mention the deal, Charlie's, iQTEC or chip volumes at all.
evidence.why_not_priced: A promise that quietly lapses generates no news event and therefore no wire copy - there is nothing for an aggregator to timestamp. If it had been priced, the stock's drift since February would show a discrete gap rather than the slow bleed the baseline records (-9.55% over 20 days, 200-day average $1.71 against a $1.42 spot), and at least one of the three posted analyst ratings would have moved off a $3.50 target.
evidence.independence: Ispire's own press-release index, a different source, shows the seven-month gap - https://www.ispiretechnology.com/press-releases (fetched 2026-09-15, listing Feb 4, Mar 11, Mar 16, May 1, May 7, May 12, Aug 17). NOTE: this finding shares the 2026-02-06 Q2 transcript with finding 1 - the shared document is the transcript, and the residual claim here (a named bilateral deal that never appeared) is distinct from the Charlie's launch slip.

evidence.text: Michael Wang - the executive who made both the chip-volume and the 'coming weeks' claims and who ran the growth narrative on the calls - was removed as Co-CEO effective 2026-07-16 and pushed down to running the Aspire North America subsidiary, disclosed in an 8-K carrying Item 5.02 only, with no Item 7.01 and no press release; three weeks later the Przybyla promotion to President got Items 5.02 AND 7.01 plus a PR Newswire release. A general web search for 'Ispire news August 2026' returns the Przybyla appointment and nothing about the CEO change. The contrasting 8-K with Item 7.01 attached is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948455/000121390026090494/ea0302192-8k_ispire.htm (2026-08-17).

evidence.text: The H1 2026 balance sheet date is 30 June 2026, which predates BOTH of Innate's cash events (the Sobi $75m upfront announced 10 Aug and the EUR 30m placement priced 14 Aug), so the headline cash line will be roughly EUR 12-13m against ~EUR 20m of financial liabilities -- i.e. negative net cash -- derived from the company's own disclosed trajectory of EUR 44.8m at 31-Dec-2025 and EUR 25.4m at 31-Mar-2026 with runway guided only to 'end of Q3 2026'.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every piece of coverage since 10 August anchors on the forward pro-forma number ('runway through Q1 2028'); no one has published the backward-looking 30-June figure the statutory H1 must actually carry, and it is the first hard cash number since 31 March. If the market had focused on it there would be a visible sell-side note reconciling June-30 cash to the pro-forma, and the stock would not be rallying into the print on 3x normal volume with no wire story. On a tape that trades ~25k ADS a day and is heavily retail, a headline 'cash position of EUR 12.x million' prints before the US open and is read literally for hours before the 08:00 EDT call reframes it.
evidence.independence: The 31-Dec-2025 anchor (EUR 44.8m cash, EUR 22.6m financial liabilities, net cash EUR 25.5m) comes from a different release: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260325193268/en/Innate-Pharma-Reports-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-and-Business-Update (2026-03-25). The EUR 70.4m at 30-Jun-2025 comparative is from https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250916779361/en/Innate-Pharma-Reports-First-Half-2025-Business-Update-and-Financial-Results (2025-09-16).

evidence.text: The Sobi USD 75m upfront -- the entire basis of the 'cash runway through Q1 2028' guidance -- is stated in the deal release as 'payable on closing', with closing 'subject to closing conditions, including the receipt of transaction related anti-trust clearance', and 37 days after signing NEITHER Innate's own press-release index NOR Sobi's carries any completion announcement.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market is carrying the 14-Aug pro-forma runway as a settled fact. It is not: if the transaction is still pending when the H1 statements are authorised for issue, the funding actually committed at that date is only ~EUR 12-13m of June-30 cash plus EUR 27.6m of net placement proceeds, i.e. ~EUR 40m against a burn that ran EUR 19.4m in Q1-2026 alone -- under twelve months, which is the specific condition that forces a going-concern material-uncertainty disclosure in a French semi-annual report reviewed by the statutory auditors. Nobody is modelling a going-concern paragraph on a stock whose last five weeks of coverage read 'funded to Q1 2028'; if they were, the 11 Aug Leerink upgrade to Outperform would have carried the condition and the stock would not have closed the gap to the EUR 1.70 placement price. This is genuinely two-sided: if the release instead announces the closing, that is a positive, which is why the band is wide and crosses zero.
evidence.independence: Sobi's own press-release index is a fully independent issuer and shows the 10 Aug signing but no closing between then and today: https://www.sobi.com/en/press-releases (checked 2026-09-16). NOTE: this finding shares the 14-Aug pricing release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001598599/000162828026057935/exhibit993.htm, 2026-08-14, 'expected to extend the Company's projected cash runway through Q1 2028') with the framing of finding 1 -- treat the Q1-2028 guidance as one document read two ways, not two pieces of evidence.

evidence.text: At the H.C. Wainwright fireside chat on 2026-09-14 management gave, for the first time publicly, a first-patient-enrolled date for the confirmatory Phase 3 TELLOMAK-3 of 'early 2027' -- against prior public guidance of trial initiation in H1 2026 (Nov-2025) and then H2 2026 (May-2026) -- and the trial still has no ClinicalTrials.gov registration of any kind.
evidence.why_not_priced: It exists only in a conference-transcript service two days old, has not appeared in any company press release, and no wire story carries it. If it were priced there would be a note cutting the lacutamab NPV for a two-quarter push of the Sezary accelerated-approval filing and of the up-to-USD-40m near-term Sobi milestones; instead the only rating action on file is an August upgrade. Formalising 'first patient early 2027' in a written H1 release converts a spoken remark into a disclosed timeline, which is when thin-tape holders act on it.
evidence.independence: A query of the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API for 'lacutamab' returns only NCT04984837, NCT03902184 and NCT05321147 -- no TELLOMAK-3 record exists, which is independent corroboration that no patient has been enrolled: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=lacutamab (checked 2026-09-16).

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: 4,986,425 shares short at the 2026-08-31 FINRA settlement, 9.6% of shares, 9.96 days to cover on FINRA's reported average daily volume; Equibles models 5,091,730 as of 2026-09-15 with the official FINRA release due 2026-09-24, i.e. after the exit window (https://equibles.com/stocks/tho/short-interest, read 2026-09-21). The sealed baseline's skew is +4.62 vol points with put/call open interest 3.01 on 1,362 contracts and priced_direction_lean 'downside paid'. Conclusion: the short book, the skew and the option open interest all point the same way, the stock is 2.6% off its 52-week low and -42% from its high, and ~10 days to cover is a real squeeze mechanism. I have therefore cut both of my negative findings (Europe -2.5 to -2.0, revenue bar -1.5 to -1.0) and let the positioning carry the emitted number above the finding sum rather than filing positioning as a finding of its own.

evidence.text: German new-registration data published by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt shows Wohnmobile down 15.7% in July 2026 and down 21.4% in August 2026 - a two-month collapse in Erwin Hymer's home market against a January-July cumulative of only -3.3% - while Thor's European segment was still shipping +4.2% units and +11.8% net sales in the February-April quarter with backlog up just 1.0%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe is where this stock's last two large negative reactions originated: 2025-12-03 -9.48% and 2026-03-03 -5.56%, both quarters in which the FY26 EPS guide was under pressure. But the line has also gone the other way: on 2026-06-03 Thor cut the FY26 EPS guide from $3.75-4.25 to $3.30-3.80 and the stock rose 2.86%, and on 2025-09-24 it set an initial FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline and rose 6.10%. This is why the size is -2.0 and not larger.
evidence.why_not_priced: The number is a single line item ('-21,4 %/1,9 %') inside a German-language KBA passenger-car press release published on 2026-09-03, eighteen days before this print. Every English-language THO preview I found anchors on RVIA wholesale and SSI retail, which are North American series; BMO's pre-print estimate cut was explicitly on 'softer retail and shipment trends' in the RV sector, i.e. the US data. The publicly circulating European datapoint is CIVD's seven-month figure of -3.0% overall and -3.3% for motor caravans, which is an order of magnitude milder than what July and August actually did, and CIVD's own Caravan Salon messaging in early September was that the industry 'expects recovery once the economic situation improves'. If the market had this, Thor's European segment - the leg that has grown net sales double digits for three straight quarters and carries ~38% of revenue - would be the thing preview notes name, and it is not. Net of the rest of the company [sizing note removed]: North America is ~62% of revenue and my read there is mildly positive, Thor Europe is taking share (24.4%, up), European backlog is +1.0% rather than falling, and the euro is roughly 3-4% stronger year on year (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/hist/dat00_eu.htm), so the reported European quarter can still be up in dollars. That is why this is filed as a guidance finding about FY27 European wholesale and not as a reported-quarter finding, and why it is sized -2.0 rather than the -4.5 the retail number alone would suggest. Caveat I am carrying explicitly: KBA's 'Wohnmobile' is a Pkw sub-category and is narrower than CIVD's 'Reisemobile', so the two series are not identical in definition.
evidence.independence: Knaus Tabbert, the listed German motorhome maker and Erwin Hymer's closest domestic competitor, reported H1 2026 revenue of EUR 503.9m, -11.9%, units -8.0%, and narrowed its FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin band to 5.0-6.0% citing 'weakened end-customer demand since spring' and 'continued cautious ordering behaviour from dealers' (https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-news-knaus-tabbert-veroeffentlicht-halbjahresfinanzbericht-2026-deutsch-543273.html, snippet_only - I read this from search output, not a successful fetch). Separately, a wave of German motorhome dealer and rental insolvencies through 2026 - Vanever/FreeVenture (7 August 2026), Schafhaeutle Reisemobile, HECK Caravan, amo caravaning, CMS Reisemobile - is documented at https://ms-aktuell.de/welt/vanever-insolvenz-wohnmobile-21-08-2026/ (2026-08-21, date confirmed in the URL path and in the body). These are different documents from the KBA release and point the same way.

evidence.text: Consensus Q4 revenue of $2.17-2.20bn requires Thor to print at or above the very top of its own unchanged FY26 guide: nine-month net sales are $7.297bn against a $9.0-9.5bn full-year range, so consensus sits at the 94th percentile of the guide while consensus EPS of $0.91-0.97 sits mid-range against the $0.71-1.21 the same guide implies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Thor's reported-quarter surprises have not been what this stock trades on: on 2026-06-03 the quarter itself was weak (North American Towable net sales -24.6%, gross margin -470bp) and the stock still rose 2.86%. The two large down days, 2025-12-03 (-9.48%) and 2026-03-03 (-5.56%), both came with guidance pressure rather than with the printed quarter alone. That is the whole reason this finding is sized -1.0 against a -3.5% fundamental read.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic off two primary documents that nobody publishes in the preview: the guide and the nine-month actuals are in the Q3 8-K, the consensus is on the wire, and the join is not. If the market had done the join, the published revenue consensus would sit near $1.95bn (the guide midpoint) rather than $2.17bn, and the revenue line would be the one the previews flagged as at-risk rather than the EPS line. What stops me sizing this larger, and I am resolving rather than leaving the contradiction to be added by the sum [sizing note removed]: a bottom-up cross-check from RVIA monthly shipments over May-July 2026 (industry -14.7%, towables ~-15.3%, motorhomes ~-10.4%) applied to Q4 FY25 segment revenue of $888.7m / $557.4m / $923.1m lands at roughly $2.15bn, essentially at consensus, while backlog-conversion off the 30 April 2026 segment backlogs (-39.1% / -13.3% / +1.0%) lands at roughly $1.96bn, essentially at the guide midpoint. The two methods bracket $1.96-2.15bn, so my honest point estimate is about $2.09bn, ~3.5% below the bar - a real but small miss, and a miss that lands inside a range the company already guided to, which [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: The FY25 Q4 segment revenue and the 31 July 2025 backlog used in the cross-check come from a different document, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/730263/000117184325006047/exh_991.htm (2025-09-24). The RVIA monthly shipment series is at https://www.rvnews.com/2026-rvia-wholesale-shipment-reports-2/ (May 22,900 -18.7%, June 25,484 -13.1%, July 19,948 -11.9%, motorhomes -25.6% in July). Note this finding shares the Q3 8-K with nothing else in this file - the backlog figures are used here only.

evidence.text: On 2026-09-10, twelve days before this print, Thor abandoned the decentralised operating model it has run for decades and put all North American RV operations under a single president and a single CFO, with the stated objective of 'drive out costs within the Company to strengthen our earnings profile' and benefits on an 'accelerated timeline' relative to the two-group structure announced earlier.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has paid for a self-help framing at a Q4 print before: on 2025-09-24, the equivalent event a year ago, Thor set an FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline off FY25's $4.85 and the stock rose 6.10%. The 2026-06-03 print, where management first put margin and cost language around a cut guide, went +2.86%. Both of the events on this line that carried a cost/structure narrative were bought.
evidence.why_not_priced: The release was filed as a leadership-change announcement and the market read it as personnel: the stock is -5.38% over the five sessions to the seal and made a new leg toward its 52-week low after it. What the document actually contains is a structural reorganisation of a famously decentralised manufacturer with an explicit margin objective and no number attached, arriving twelve days before the one print of the year at which this company sets full-year guidance. If the market had priced it you would expect the pre-print drift to be positive rather than -5.38%, and you would expect at least one of the three pre-print analyst actions I could find (BofA target $96 to $86 on 2026-09-21, BMO estimate cuts, Wall Street Zen to Sell on 2026-09-20) to frame FY27 around a cost programme rather than around 'softer retail and shipment trends'. The inference I am making - that the FY27 guide arrives with a quantified structural-savings element - is an inference and not a disclosed number, which is why this is +1.5 and not larger.
evidence.independence: The earlier two-group reorganisation is a separate release at https://ir.thorindustries.com/investor-resources/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/THOR-INDUSTRIES-ANNOUNCES-STRATEGIC-EVOLUTION-OF-NORTH-AMERICAN-OPERATING-MODEL-WITH-FORMATION-OF-TWO-RV-GROUPS/default.aspx (date not independently confirmed by me; the 2026-09-10 release references it as 'previously announced'). Corroborating, the Indiana Department of Workforce Development's current WARN list carries no 2026 notice from any Thor entity (https://www.in.gov/dwd/warn-notices/current-warn-notices/, read 2026-09-21) despite a 25% decline in towable unit shipments - Thor has been taking cost out through structure rather than through plant closures, which is consistent with the operating-model route and inconsistent with a capacity-cut route.

evidence.text: Camping World, Thor's largest customer and holder of record US new-unit share above 29%, exited its June 2026 quarter with new vehicles on the lot down ~17% year on year in units (dollars down only ~5%), prior-model-year exposure on new RVs near 1% against over 6% a year earlier, and units aged more than 365 days cut by over 60%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Thor's FY26 has been a story of the towable guide being cut on 'cautious independent dealer ordering patterns' (2026-06-03 release); the 2025-09-24 Q4 print noted the opposite - 'initiatives to gain market share began to deliver results' with towable wholesale -10.1% - and the stock rose 6.10%. A dealer-restock framing at a Q4 print has been bought on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and I am sizing it accordingly at +1.0. This is a direct counterparty speaking after Thor last guided [sizing note removed], and it is the single largest offset to the 'channel is still stuffed' read that the RVIA-minus-SSI gap generates - US retail registrations ran -19.0% in May and -20.7% in June against wholesale of -18.7% and -13.1%, which looks like inventory building until you find that the largest single buyer's lot is 17% lighter in units with almost no carryover model years. The reason it is not fully in the price is that it is eight weeks old, sits in a competitor's transcript rather than in any THO preview, and cuts against the direction every RV headline since has taken. If the market had folded it in, the pre-print commentary would be about a 2027 restock rather than about 'softer retail and shipment trends'. Marked snippet_only: I read the inventory figures from search output of the Q2 2026 call, not from a successful fetch of the transcript.
evidence.independence: The quarter itself is in the primary 8-K exhibit at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001669779/000110465926088141/cwh-20260729xex99d1.htm (2026-07-29), a different document from the transcript. Pointing the same way from a third party, Patrick Industries put dealer field inventory at roughly 18-20 weeks on hand against a pre-2020 norm of 26-30 weeks on its Q2 2026 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/patrick-industries-patk-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/, 2026-07-30). Pointing the other way, and I am netting it out rather than filing it separately: the same Patrick call cut its CY2026 RV wholesale forecast to 285,000-300,000 units, below RVIA's own Summer RoadSigns range of 300,000-328,100 (https://www.rvtrader.com/blog/2026/07/13/rvia-lowers-2026-rv-wholesale-shipment-forecast/).

evidence.text: FINRA's short-interest settlement for 2026-09-15 publishes on 2026-09-24, two sessions after the exit. Equibles models 5,091,730 shares short, +2.1% on the 2026-08-31 figure of 4,986,425 - shorts still building into the print - but the confirmation the market can trade on arrives after the window closes.

RVIA's August 2026 wholesale shipment report is not yet published as of 2026-09-21 - the RVIA reports page still shows July 2026 (19,948 units, 183,592 YTD) as the latest. It is the first read on Thor's FQ1 FY27 and on whether July's -25.6% motorhome print was an outlier, and it will land after this trade is closed.

The all-stock Patrick Industries / LCI Industries merger, targeting $150m of net annual run-rate cost savings, is expected to close in H1 2027. It consolidates two of Thor's three largest component suppliers into one counterparty and is a structural input cost question for FY27-28, not for this print.

Indiana Department of Workforce Development current WARN notices for 2026: no notice from any Thor entity (Jayco, Keystone, Heartland, Cruiser RV, DRV, Airstream, KZ, Thor Motor Coach, Tiffin, Entegra, Dutchmen, CrossRoads, Highland Ridge) despite a 25% decline in towable unit shipments. The only 2026 Elkhart-county RV closure on the list is Forest River Plant 63, Bristol, 105 jobs, notice 2026-07-17, effective 2026-09-17 - Forest River is a Berkshire Hathaway company and not a Thor subsidiary, and at least one widely-shared September article implies otherwise (https://hoodline.com/2026/09/elkhart-county-rv-plant-closure-cuts-105-jobs-as-tariffs-squeeze-indiana-manufacturing/). No finding either way.

Insider activity: only three Form 4s in calendar 2026 (2026-01-16, 2026-03-09, 2026-06-17) and one Form 5 on 2026-09-02. No cluster, no pattern, nothing to size. https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000730263&type=4&dateb=&owner=only&count=20

IEEPA tariff refunds: the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and the CIT has ordered roughly $165bn of refunds, but I could find no Thor-specific receivable, claim or accrual in the 30 April 2026 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000730263/000073026326000018/tho-20260430.htm) or in any 8-K, and Thor's Q3 commentary still describes tariffs as a live cost headwind rather than a recovery. Thor is mostly not the importer of record. Worth 0.

Thor 8-K flow since the last print: two filings, and the only substantive one is the routine $0.52 quarterly dividend declared 2026-06-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/730263/000073026326000021/tho-20260616.htm). No financing event, no covenant amendment, no buyback authorisation change to ask [sizing note removed].

A dedicated company-level European disclosure for Erwin Hymer - registrations, order intake or dealer inventory - does not exist; CIVD's own market-data page carries only 2025 annual figures (https://www.civd.de/en/artikel/european-market/), which is why the KBA monthly series had to carry the European finding.
August 2026 RVIA wholesale shipments and the RVIA monthly seals report: not published or not publicly reachable as of 2026-09-21.
A second corroborating source for short interest: fintel.io returned HTTP 403 and capedge.com HTTP 404 to WebFetch.

history.basis: 6-K exhibit text matched results language (4 filings opened). Heuristic, not an item code: a 6-K carrying results language is very likely an earnings release but this is weaker than the 8-K item 2.02 path

event_plausibility.reason: inferred cadence of 61 days is too short to be an earnings cadence (quarterly is ~91, semi-annual ~182), so the 3 matched filings are not earnings -- most likely monthly operational updates caught by the 6-K text matcher. No cadence verdict is possible and the reaction history above should not be used as an earnings base rate. Confirm the date from a company source instead.

baseline.deadband_basis: half the median of 3 prior reactions, floored at 1.5%
baseline.deadband_note: A realised move inside this band is scored as no-direction rather than as a miss.
baseline.expected_move_basis: median historical reaction (no usable option chain)

baseline_quality.note: thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced, so a confident call on this name cannot be justified by the baseline.

first_hunter_context.bar: Company's own guide: Q4 FY2026 revenue of RMB130.0-140.0 million (midpoint 135) and FY2026 revenue of RMB600.0-610.0 million, both set in the Q3 FY2026 release of 2026-06-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1932770/000121390026065474/ea029361801ex99-1.htm . The FY range is purely additive (Q1 127.1 + Q2 177.3 + Q3 164.7 = 469.1, plus the Q4 guide = 599.1-609.1), so it carries no cushion of its own. first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 548,832 shares, 2.68% of shares outstanding, short ratio 29.99 days to cover, float 18.74m of 54.38m shares -- https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/here/statistics/ read 2026-09-21. As a percentage of shares out that is not crowded, but 30 days to cover on a ~20,677-share ADV means a covering short is mechanically a squeeze, which is a reason to shrink a negative here. There is NO options market (baseline options.status = no_options_market), so there is no skew and no implied move -- the market makes no directional statement about this print at all, and I have no anchor for what is priced beyond the tape: run_up_20d -1.62%, run_up_5d -3.19%, i.e. flat and unpositioned into the event. Largest disclosed holder KPartners Limited / Rui Zhang at 23,170,342 Class A shares (14.2%), routine quarterly 13G/A, event date 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-11, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001932770/000172704226000003/primary_doc.xml -- no 13D and no activist.

evidence.text: Management has beaten the midpoint of its own quarterly revenue guide by +14.4% and +13.6% in the two immediately preceding quarters (Q2 guided RMB150-160m on 2025-12-02, printed RMB177.3m; Q3 guided RMB140-150m on 2026-03-12, printed RMB164.7m), and the Q4 guide of RMB130-140m was set on 2026-06-05 with two of the quarter's three months already elapsed -- so Q4 revenue should land near RMB148-155m and FY2026 revenue above the top of the revised RMB600-610m range.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This exact line has been sold twice in a row: the Q2 print beat its guided range by 14.4% and the stock fell 16.26% (2026-03-12); the Q3 print beat its guided range by 13.6%, the CFO's own quote said results 'exceeded expectations on both revenue and gross margin', and the stock fell 24.89% (2026-06-05, close 2.37 -> 1.78 on 431,500 shares). A revenue beat against this company's own guide has a 0-for-2 record of paying, which is why this is [sizing note removed].5 and not at the beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every piece of English wire copy on this name leads with the 22% FY guidance cut, not with the fact that the company has beaten each of the two quarterly ranges it set since. If the pattern were priced, the stock would not be at 1.08x net cash with EV of US$8.3m and a single broker at a $2.50 target; you would also see some run-up into the print, and the tape is -1.62% over 20 sessions on 20,677 shares a day. The three data points have to be assembled from three separate releases; no aggregator carries guide-vs-actual for this name.
evidence.independence: Q1 FY26 release giving the Q2 guide: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/12/02/3197667/0/en/Here-Announces-Unaudited-Financial-Results-for-the-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026.html ; Q2 FY26 release giving the Q3 guide and the Q2 actual: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1932770/000121390026026610/ea028104301ex99-1.htm . NOTE: this finding and finding 2 rest on the same two quarters' releases read two different ways (one as a guidance-setting pattern, one as a reaction record); I have shrunk this one to +0.5 to avoid counting the same two quarters twice.

evidence.text: The baseline's reaction history is wrong and the real one is far worse and far larger: rebuilt from confirmed release dates, this stock has fallen on 4 of 4 earnings prints -- 2025-09-17 (FY25 annual, bmo) -2.07%, 2025-12-02 -3.78%, 2026-03-12 -16.26%, 2026-06-05 -24.89% -- and the accessible wire copy misreports the 2026-06-05 move as -5.68% when the daily bars show 2.37 -> 1.78.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding IS the reaction history. The baseline carries median_abs_move_pct 3.78 and expected_move_pct 3.78 off three 6-K text matches on an inferred 61-day cadence it calls implausible; the sweep flagged baseline_history_trustworthy: false. Rebuilt from the four confirmed releases (2025-09-17, 2025-12-02, 2026-03-12, 2026-06-05) the median absolute reaction is ~10% and the two most recent prints, both under the pop-toy-only business, are -16.26% and -24.89%. The mean is -11.75%. No print has been up.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no option chain on this name, so there is no implied move for anyone to have marked to this distribution, and the one aggregator statement I could find prices the June reaction at -5.68% -- a fifth of what actually happened. The only anchor anyone else has is the same 3.78% median the sealed baseline built from non-earnings 6-Ks. If the market were carrying a 10-25% event distribution you would see it in the tape into the print; instead the stock is dead flat on 20k shares a day. A shareholder base that has sold this name on every print including two revenue beats is a mechanism, not a mood.
evidence.independence: Same measurement on three other windows from the same price source, each cross-checked against a confirmed release date: 2026-03-12 gives -16.37% against the baseline's independently computed -16.26% (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HERE?period1=1773014400&period2=1773532800&interval=1d) and 2025-12-02 gives -3.78%, matching the baseline exactly (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HERE?period1=1764201600&period2=1765065600&interval=1d), which validates the date mapping used for the June figure. The 2025-09-17 annual print is confirmed as a real event by https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/11/3148378/0/en/QuantaSing-to-Report-Fourth-Fiscal-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Financial-Results-on-September-17-2025.html . Shares the two Q2/Q3 releases with finding 1; the price series is a different source.

evidence.text: The equity is a cash box with a live buyback the size of a fifth of itself: net cash US$91.76m against a US$100.07m market cap (EV US$8.31m), a new US$20.0m repurchase authorisation running 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30 that was announced with the guidance cut, US$12.8m already spent of the prior US$20m programme, and a board with form for autumn capital return (US$11m special dividend declared 2024-10-01). The FY release is where usage of the 2026 programme gets disclosed.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 buyback was announced on 2026-06-05 inside the guidance-cut release and the stock still fell 24.89%, so an authorisation alone has demonstrably bought nothing here. What has never been tested at this price is a disclosed repurchase figure or a distribution: the only cash distribution in the company's history (2024-10-01, US$0.067/ordinary, US$0.201/ADS, ~US$11m) came two weeks after an annual results release, not inside one.
evidence.why_not_priced: At 1.08x net cash with EV of US$8.3m the market is explicitly pricing the cash to be burned rather than returned; that is the price statement, and any disclosure that contradicts it is unpriced by construction. A US$20m authorisation is 20% of the market cap and ~59% of the float's market value on a name trading US$38k a day -- if it were credited, the stock could not sit at 1.08x cash with no bid. Nobody models this: one broker, no options, no run-up.
evidence.independence: The 2026 authorisation and the US$12.8m spent under the 2025 programme as of 2026-06-01 are in the company's own Q3 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1932770/000121390026065474/ea029361801ex99-1.htm ; the special-dividend precedent is a separate release, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/10/01/2955953/0/en/QuantaSing-Announces-Declaration-of-a-Special-Dividend.html . I deliberately dropped the one supporting item that was inference rather than document -- July 2026 volume averaged ~56,000 shares/day against ~18,600 in August (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/here/history/) which is consistent with company buying but is not evidence of it, and a volume series is not a company number.

evidence.text: Two forward items surfaced in Chinese-language media in the ten days before the print and appear in no English coverage: the fifth-generation WAKUKU line '怪上头' went on sale offline on 2026-09-21 with the online drop at 20:00 Beijing on 2026-09-22 (the day of the call), and at CIFTIS on 2026-09-11 the company said overseas is ~20% of group annual revenue, products sell into 27 countries, and its target is overseas sales of 3-5x the prior year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Untested on this line at this name: the initial FY guide given at the last annual print (FY26 RMB750-800m, 2025-09-17) produced only -2.07%, the smallest reaction of the four, and it was then cut 22% eight months later -- so this shareholder base did not pay for an optimistic initial guide and was later proved right not to. Tomorrow's release should carry an initial FY2027 guide on the same template, and that, not the Q4 number, is the line that will set the move.
evidence.why_not_priced: Both are Chinese-language only; there is no English wire item, no broker note and no aggregator entry for either, and a $38k/day ADR's marginal holder is not reading Tencent News. If they were priced you would see some bid into a print that is instead flat on the 5- and 20-day tape. A company that sends staff to a trade fair on 2026-09-11 to talk about a 3-5x overseas target and drops a fifth-generation flagship line the morning of its own call is not, on the face of it, about to guide FY2027 down -- though this is a target and a launch, not a number, which is why it is [sizing note removed].5.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The directly comparable event is last year's full-year print, 2025-09-17: Q4 FY2025 revenue GBP164.1m against a GBP169.96m estimate, a 3.4% miss, with adjusted EPS of -3.16p against +7.14p expected, and the stock fell roughly 7.4% in pre-market (https://www.chartmill.com/news/MANU/Chartmill-34431-Manchester-United-PLC---CL-A-NYSEMANU-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Earnings-Misses-EPS-Estimates). [sizing note removed].5 because it lands INSIDE a range the company published four months ago [sizing note removed] and because a crowded short is a reason to shrink a negative [sizing note removed].
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a two-analyst name and the consensus is a mechanical -9.76% year-on-year roll of last year's GBP164.1m Q4 rather than a residual off the company's own guide; if the market had done the subtraction, the previews would be framing a GBP135-145m quarter rather than quoting GBP148.17m as the number to beat, and the FY estimate would not sit at exactly the top of a range the company gave itself. evidence.independence: Two independent estimate sources agree on the level being above the guide-implied maximum — Investing.com's GBP148.17m (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/manchester-united-earnings-on-deck-champions-league-boost-in-focus-93CH-4911041, 2026-09-22) and the $192.226m carried by the Nasdaq/MarketBeat feed. evidence.text: Two commercial deals were signed AFTER the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet date and after the company last gave guidance on 27 May 2026, and both land only in the FY2027 outlook this release will introduce: a Betway training-kit partnership at a record ~GBP20m a year, which the club itself calls the biggest training-kit deal in world football (4 August 2026), and a SumUp shirt-sleeve deal the club calls its biggest ever sleeve partnership, against a prior DXC sleeve deal in the GBP10-20m a season range (8 September 2026).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock has actually paid on. On 2026-05-27, the one unambiguous earnings reaction in the baseline, Manchester United raised FY2026 revenue guidance to GBP655-665m and adjusted EBITDA to GBP200-210m and the stock rose +12.68% — the largest move in the eight-row history by a factor of nearly three. The 2025-09-17 full-year print guided FY2026 to GBP640-660m, BELOW the GBP666.5m just reported, and fell ~7.4%. Same name, same line, opposite signs, both double-digit-capable: the guide direction is the reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Both were sponsorship-trade and football-press stories, not financial-wire stories, and the equity market visibly did not reprice on them: the stock fell in 9 of the 10 sessions to 2026-09-10 and is -13.76% over 20 sessions, straight through the 8 September SumUp announcement, and is -15.5% from its 52-week high. With two analysts covering and the last published model dated 27 May 2026 (Seeking Alpha's FY27 build, which lists only Champions League money, sporting bonuses and the Adidas clause), no sell-side FY2027 number can contain either deal. Combined they are roughly GBP20-30m of incremental, near-100%-margin annual commercial revenue against an adjusted EBITDA base of GBP200-210m.
